data.title: Show HN: McWig – A modal, Vim-like text editor written in Go
data.author: andrew_bbb
data.article_summary: McWig是一个由Go语言编写的模态文本编辑器，类似Vim，目前是早期开发阶段，主要用于编辑`.go`文件。它具备LSP自动补全、跳转定义、悬停信息、Tree-sitter支持、颜色主题、宏录制等功能，但存在较多漏洞。键位绑定大多模仿Vim，支持基本的代码编辑操作。项目初衷是快速探索文本编辑器的实现，未来计划发展为稳定、功能齐全的编辑器。当前仅为实验性项目，使用时需注意文件备份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个新的代码编辑器项目的功能、可用性、扩展性以及与Vim、Helix等已有编辑器的比较。

不同观点：
• [GuiShou] 认为该项目虽然是“玩具”项目，但其可用性已经通过日常使用得到了验证。他们对学习曲线、类Org模式功能以及是否支持插件表示关注，并对借鉴Helix的颜色主题设计表示赞赏。
• [xlii] 提到了另一个类似编辑器Anvil Editor，强调其受ACME启发、开放源代码以及可组合性，并指出其通过REST API与外部工具交互的功能。
• [paddy_m] 对Vim家族的扩展性提出疑问，并以Emacs为例，说明其通过Lisp解释器实现扩展的方式，暗示对该项目扩展性的关注。
• [scuff3d] 对项目中的bug持宽容态度，表示有兴趣探索代码库。
• [imiric] 赞赏项目的同时，特别关注其未来的扩展性，并建议利用现有生态系统的插件以避免从零开始。
• [nickandbrock] 对项目的颜色主题表示赞赏，并提到自己的项目，表示可能会借鉴该项目的颜色设计。
• [lsllc] 对项目使用diff进行撤销/重做的设计表示赞赏。
• [wyclif] 以幽默的方式建议改名，未提出功能性意见。
• [hit8run] 表示支持并鼓励项目继续发展，提到自己目前使用Helix作为终端代码编辑器，并愿意尝试该新项目。
• [tempfile] 关注该项目与Vim的不同之处，询问其相比Vim更有效的功能特点。

补充讨论：
• 项目的扩展性是讨论的焦点之一，多位评论者（paddy_m, imiric）对此表示关注，并以Vim和Emacs为例进行比较。
• 颜色主题和用户界面设计得到了多位评论者的赞赏（GuiShou, nickandbrock）。
• 不同编辑器之间的比较和借鉴（如Helix和Anvil Editor）也是讨论的一个重要方面（GuiShou, xlii）。
• 项目的创新性设计（如使用diff进行撤销/重做）引起了积极的反响（lsllc）。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明显的争议，但扩展性问题是一个潜在的讨论热点，涉及到项目未来的发展方向和生态建设。

McWig (temporary name)
Hi! Welcome to my text editor page.
McWig is a modal, Vim-like text editor written in Go. I use it as my daily driver, btw.
Note:
McWig currently supports only
.go
files. Do not edit files that are not backed up. McWig is still in an early stage of development and may damage your files.
Features
LSP autocomplete, goto definition, hover info
Tree-sitter support
Color themes (borrowed from the Helix text editor)
Lots of bugs
Macro support
Something like Emacs org-mode: Open
test.txt
, place the cursor at line 15, and press
"Ctrl-C Ctrl-C"
.
This project was written as a "speed run" — not for speed in terms of time, but rather as an exercise to explore the text editor problem space without overthinking or planning ahead. It’s a quick and "dirty" implementation, so to speak.
Running
make setup-runtime
make build-run
Keybindings
Most common Vim keybindings are implemented, providing minimal but enough (for me) support for daily source code editing. See
config/config.go
for all implemented keybindings.
To get started:

Description

Plans
I plan to turn this "toy project" into a stable, fully-featured Vim-like text editor.

data.title: Slow and steady, this poem will win your heart
data.author: mrholme
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对特定网页设计和诗歌内容的感受与解读

不同观点：
• Noelia- 认为网页设计初看有些 awkward，但随着时间推移，这种节奏变得合适。她指出这种设计让读者放慢速度，对于这首诗来说是有效的，虽然不会立刻吸引人，但若耐心阅读几分钟，会逐渐产生共鸣。

• b0a04gl 引用诗中的一段，解读其深层含义，认为诗中表达的是一种深层次的无力感，即人们不仅无法赢得改变，甚至不认为自己有机会参与其中，这种心态非常深刻。

• jihadjihad 提供了诗歌的原始文本链接，指出这首诗创作于1994年，将讨论引向诗歌本身的创作时间。

• zem 对诗中的特定词汇 "shell-y skylark" 表示赞赏，认为其使用非常巧妙。

• dash2 提供了另一首关于弱小缓慢生物的诗歌链接，并指出其中含有战争的暗示，试图引导讨论向其他相关诗歌扩展。

• tptacek 提出一个质疑，询问为什么特别选择这首诗进行讨论，表现出对选择这首诗的原因感兴趣。

• darepublic 引用诗中的一句话 "Patience, the sport of truly chastened things" 作为回应，似乎以此表达对诗歌主题的理解或共鸣。

• neonate 提供了一个存档链接，但没有进一步的解释或讨论。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了诗歌的深层解读，特别是对诗中表达的无助感和心理状态的分析（b0a04gl）。
• 部分用户分享了相关诗歌链接（dash2）和原始文本链接（jihadjihad），扩展了讨论的范围。
• 用户对网页设计的体验分享（Noelia-）引发了对这种设计选择是否有效的思考。
• 存在对诗歌选择原因的质疑（tptacek），表明讨论中有人对背景或动机感兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点可能在于为什么特别选择这首诗进行讨论（tptacek 的提问），以及这种网页设计是否真正有效，尽管 Noelia- 认为最终有效，但初看时感到 awkward。

data.title: Show HN: I wrote a BitTorrent Client from scratch
data.author: piyushgupta53
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个用Go语言实现的BitTorrent客户端——go-torrent-client。该项目实现了BitTorrent客户端的核心功能，包括种子文件解析、节点发现与通信以及文件下载。主要特性包括Bencode编码/解码、种子文件处理、节点发现与通信、以及下载管理（如分片和块管理、进度跟踪等）。项目结构清晰，包含命令行界面、内部包（如Bencode编码、种子处理、节点协议等）以及公共包。目前该项目正在积极开发中，未来计划支持磁力链接、元数据交换协议和DHT。需要Go 1.21或更高版本进行安装和使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言实现的BitTorrent客户端的实现细节、安全性、功能完整性及潜在改进方向

不同观点：
• [jorkingit] 认为需要限制bencode解码器中的动态分配大小，以防止恶意输入通过请求极大的分配来导致拒绝服务（DoS）攻击。建议将剩余的输入长度作为上限。
• [vkaku] 对项目表示赞赏，并建议在README中添加简单的使用说明，例如如何通过命令行下载.torrent文件。此外，还建议添加从URL解析torrent文件的功能。
• [__jonas] 提到一个名为codecrafters的平台，该平台提供相关课程并包含测试，可以作为实现BitTorrent客户端的指导。
• [ashirviskas] 作为一个非Go开发者，询问为什么使用较旧的Go版本1.21，并指出该版本已在10个月前被弃用。
• [agiron123] 表示该项目让他们回想起大学时的网络课程项目，并认为这种项目是学习新语言的好方法。
• [vivzkestrel] 对项目的构建过程表示好奇，询问作者是参考了协议文档还是通过其他实现来构建项目。

补充讨论：
• [NooneAtAll3] 询问是否支持磁力链接，并在编辑中提到这似乎是一个计划中的功能。
• [TheEdonian] 询问为该项目添加图形用户界面（GUI）的难度，并表示对Go语言的GUI实现不熟悉。
• [throwaway894345] 对项目的完整性和处理复杂功能（如DHT、磁力链接、NAT traversal）的能力表示关注，并询问项目的完成度和实现难度。
• [NoMoreNicksLeft] 询问是否实现了v2和可变torrent，并表示对可变torrent的支持非常重要。
• [OccamsMirror] 询问该项目是否可以作为库使用。
• [b0a04gl] 认为项目在崩溃恢复、加密握手、uTP支持和NAT行为等方面缺乏说明，并指出在真实环境中可能存在风险。建议增加模块化设计和内存保护机制，并提到需要一个roadmap。

争议焦点：
• 项目的安全性和功能完整性是主要争议点。一些评论者关注项目在处理恶意输入、复杂BitTorrent功能（如DHT、磁力链接）、以及在真实环境中的稳定性方面的能力。
• 另外，使用较旧的Go版本也引起了一些讨论。

Go-Torrent
A BitTorrent client implementation in Go that supports downloading files using the BitTorrent protocol. This project implements the core functionality of a BitTorrent client, including torrent file parsing, peer discovery, and file downloading.
Features
Bencode Encoding/Decoding
Support for all Bencode types (strings, integers, lists, dictionaries)
Robust error handling and validation
Torrent File Processing
Parse .torrent files (both single-file and multi-file torrents)
Info hash calculation
Piece hash extraction
Support for all standard torrent file fields
Peer Discovery and Communication
HTTP tracker support
Peer handshake protocol
Complete BitTorrent message protocol
Peer connection management
Download Functionality
Piece and block management
Concurrent downloads
Progress tracking
File assembly for both single and multi-file torrents
Storage management with block-level granularity
Project Structure
.
├── cmd/          # Command-line interface and main application
├── internal/     # Internal packages
│   ├── bencode/  # Bencode encoding/decoding
│   ├── torrent/  # Torrent file processing
│   ├── tracker/  # Tracker protocol implementation
│   ├── peer/     # Peer communication
│   └── download/ # Download management
└── pkg/          # Public packages
Requirements
Go 1.21 or later
Installation
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/go-torrent.git
cd

data.author: tombh
data.article_summary: Tattoy是一个为现代终端设计的文本 compositor，通过GPU渲染着色器并提供TTY滚动缓冲区的实时更新小地图。它基于纯文本，适用于任何支持真彩色的终端模拟器，利用UTF8半块字符（▀, ▄）实现图形效果。其主要功能包括自动调整文本对比度、运行背景命令（如音频可视化、视频背景、系统监控图表）、以及自定义插件支持。Tattoy兼容Shader Toy和Ghostty着色器，并且可以在正常终端状态和特效之间快速切换。此外，它还管理自己的滚动缓冲区，并提供滚动条功能，确保文本对比度易读。插件可以通过JSON协议进行开发，支持任意语言。

A Text-Based Compositor For Modern Terminals
Tattoy with a GPU-rendered shader and live-updating minimap of the TTY scrollback.
About
Tattoy can generally be thought of as a framework for adding eye-candy to your terminal. It is purely text-based so works in any terminal emulator that supports true colour. "Graphics" is rendered with UTF8 half-blocks (▀,▄). Whilst most of its effects are for getting you street credibility it also has more powerful features based around its awareness of terminal contents. For example it can detect and auto adjust text contrast whilst remaining faithful to the terminal's palette.
Tattoy works with your existing shell, theme and prompt, etc. It can always and immediately toggle between its effects and your normal terminal state, allowing for easy copy-pasting for example.
Shaders
Perhaps the fanciest feature of Tattoy is its ability to render GPU shaders. It is designed to be able to run most shaders from
Shader Toy
without any editing at all. It also supports
Ghostty shaders
out-of-the-box, though certain shaders that alter the position of text (such as CRT emulators) don't have a pronounced impact as text rendering is always left to the host terminal emulator.
Second Terminal In Background
You can run an arbitrary command that is rendered in the background of your normal terminal. Use-cases for this might be:
an audio visualiser
video background
system monitor graphs
The background terminal's opacity can be adjusted so it doesn't visual conflict too much with your actual terminal.
Scrollback Minimap
The minimap is a pixelised version of the contents of the scrollback, including the current contents of the screen. It live updates, even when using the so-called "alternate screen" for apps like `nvim`, `top`, `gitui`, etc.
Tattoy manages its own scrollback buffer (like say `tmux` does), and so can therefore also provide its own scrollbar.
Auto Text Contrast
Have you ever run `ls` in a directory only for certain file types to be completely illegible? This has long been an intractable problem caused by the limited colours of terminal palettes. CLI applications are only ever aware of palette index values, not the underlying RGB value, therefore it is impossible for them to know if any given background colour is sufficient enough to allow its containing text to be readable.
Not anymore!
Tattoy is aware of the true 24 bit RGBA value of all colours in your terminal. This allows it to use clever algorithms to detect low contrast text and auto adjust the foreground colour within the constraints of your chosen terminal theme to find the nearest colour that meets a minimum contrast threshold.
Plugins
Plugins can be written in any language. You get full access to your terminal's contents and can render both UTF8 "pixels" and text to a dedicated plugin layer of your choosing. Currently the protocol is JSON over `STDIN` and `STDOUT`. See the
plugin documentation
for more info.
Here we see the cursor giving off smoke particles that interact with the terminal's text. The source code can be found
here
.

data.title: OxCaml - a set of extensions to the OCaml programming language.
data.author: lairv
data.article_summary:
OxCaml 是 OCaml 编程语言的一套快速发展的扩展，由 Jane Street 开发，旨在提升 OCaml 在性能导向编程中的表现。OxCaml 的设计目标是提供安全、便捷、可预测的控制，特别是在性能关键的程序行为方面，且仅在需要时引入复杂性。它保持与 OCaml 的兼容性，所有有效的 OCaml 程序也是有效的 OxCaml 程序。

OxCaml 的扩展包括：
1. **无畏并发**：通过类型系统静态排除数据竞争。
2. **内存布局**：允许指定数据在内存中的布局，并支持 SIMD 处理器扩展。
3. **控制分配**：提供工具减少垃圾回收压力，提高缓存效率和确定性。
4. **生活质量改进**：如多态参数、包含函子、标记元组和不可变数组。

OxCaml 是开源的，但其扩展不保证稳定性或向后兼容性。它提供了与标准 OCaml 工具集兼容的修改版本，方便用户使用。Jane Street 还开源了一些库和工具，部分扩展仅在 OxCaml 中可用。

44268782.article_content:
OxCaml
OxCaml is a fast-moving set of extensions to the OCaml programming language.
It is both Jane Street’s production compiler, as well as a laboratory for experiments focused towards making
OCaml better for performance-oriented programming. Our hope is that these extensions can over time be
contributed to upstream OCaml.
OxCaml’s primary design goals are:
to provide
safe, convenient, predictable
control over performance-critical
aspects
of
program behavior
but
only where you need it,
and…
in OCaml!
Let’s talk about what this means!
OxCaml’s extensions are meant to make OCaml a great language for performance engineering. Performance
engineering
requires control, and we want that control to be:
Safe. Safety is a critical feature for making programmers more productive, and for shipping correct
code.
Languages that are pervasively unsafe are too hard to use correctly.
Convenient. We want to provide control without bewildering programmers, or drowning them in endless
annotations.
To achieve this, we aim to maintain OCaml’s excellent type-inference, even as we add considerable
expressiveness
to the type-system.
Predictable. One of the great features of OCaml today is that it’s pretty easy to look at OCaml code and
understand how it’s going to perform. We want our extensions to maintain and improve on that property,
by
making
key performance details explicit at the type-level.
By "only where you need it", we mean that OxCaml’s extensions should be pay-as-you-go. While OxCaml aims to
provide
more power to optimize, you shouldn’t need to swallow extra complexity when you’re not using that power.
By "in OCaml", we mean that all valid OCaml programs are also valid OxCaml programs. But our more profound
goal
is
for OxCaml to feel like OCaml evolving into a better version of itself, rather than a new language. For
that,
OxCaml
needs to honor OCaml’s basic design sensibility, and to preserve the safety, ease, and productivity that are
hallmarks of the language.
OxCaml’s extensions
Our extensions can be roughly organized into a few areas:
Fearless concurrency
Writing correct concurrent programs is notoriously difficult. OxCaml includes additions to the
type
system to
statically rule out data races.
Layouts
OxCaml lets programmers specify the way their data is laid out in memory. It also provides native
access
to
SIMD processor extensions.
Control over allocation
OxCaml gives programmers tools to control allocations, reducing GC pressure and making programs
more
cache efficient and deterministic.
Quality of life
OxCaml also contains some extensions that aren’t specifically about systems programming, but
which
we’ve
found helpful in our day-to-day work:
Polymorphic parameters
Include functor
Labeled tuples
Immutable arrays
Using OxCaml
OxCaml is open-source, and we’re excited to welcome experimental users, especially researchers and tinkerers
who
can
kick the tires and provide feedback on the system. We put the emphasis on experimental because OxCaml makes
no
promises of stability or backwards compatibility for its extensions (though it does remain backwards
compatible
with
OCaml).
OxCaml is intended to be easy to use, and to that end comes with modified versions of the standard OCaml
tool-set,
including:
Package management, compatible with dune and opam
Editor integration via the LSP-server
Source code formatting
Documentation generation
Jane Street has long open sourced a bunch of useful libraries and tools. These are now released in two forms:
one
for
upstream OCaml, in which our extensions have been stripped, and one for OxCaml, where the extensions are
fully
leveraged.
Not all extensions are erasable, so some libraries will be available only for OxCaml. We’ll export
OCaml-compatible
versions of these libraries when the necessary extensions are integrated upstream.

Abstract:
In this work, we show how Euclidean 3-space uniquely emerges from the structure of quantum temporal correlations associated with sequential measurements of Pauli observables on a single qubit. Quite remarkably, the quantum temporal correlations which give rise to geometry are independent of the initial state of the qubit, which we show enables an observer to extract geometric data from sequential measurements without the observer having any knowledge of initial conditions. Such results suggest the plausibility that space itself may emerge from quantum temporal correlations, and we formulate a toy model of such a hypothetical phenomenon.

data.title: The Missing Manual for Signals: State Management for Python Developers
data.author: buibuibui
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种用于Python中的响应式状态管理工具——`reaktiv`，并讨论了何时需要使用这种工具。传统的状态管理方式在处理多组件状态同步或维护手动协调时可能变得复杂且容易出错。文章指出，当状态变化需要在多个组件中传递，或手动更新变得难以维护时，响应式编程（如信号系统）可以有效解决这些问题。

文章详细分析了传统状态管理的弊端，如隐式依赖、紧密耦合、不一致状态窗口和测试复杂性等问题，并提出了响应式状态管理（信号）的解决方案。信号通过显式依赖关系图自动处理状态更新，避免了手动维护带来的潜在错误。

本文还提供了在现有系统中逐步采用信号的方法、常见模式与反模式，以及性能和测试方面的考虑。最终，文章帮助开发者判断何时应采用响应式状态管理，何时则不必。

A practical guide to reactive state management in Python
Introduction
I maintain
reaktiv
. When I demo it to Python teams, I get the same response: "Why do I need this? I can just call functions when things change."
Fair question. Python has excellent patterns for coordinating state changes. You can trigger updates manually, use the observer pattern, or set up event systems. Most Python applications handle state coordination just fine.
But some don't.
If you're building systems where state changes cascade through multiple components, where derived values need to stay synchronized, or where manual coordination is becoming a maintenance burden - signals might solve real problems for you.
Frontend developers recognize the pattern immediately. They've dealt with forgetting to trigger updates when state changes, or having component state get out of sync. Signals solve the "forgot to update X when Y changed" class of bugs.
This manual shows you when that coordination problem is worth solving with reactive programming, and when it's not.
What You'll Learn
When reactive state management solves real problems (and when it doesn't)
How to adopt signals incrementally in existing systems
Patterns that work in production Python applications
Let's start with what breaks as state coordination scales.
Table of Contents
The Problem with Traditional State Management
What Are Signals, Really?
The Mental Model Shift
When Signals Matter (And When They Don't)
Common Patterns and Anti-Patterns
Real-World Scenarios
Performance Considerations
Integration Strategies
Testing Reactive Code
Migration Guide
The Problem with Traditional State Management
As developers, we've all written variations of this code:
class OrderService:
def __init__(self):
self.orders = []
self.total_revenue = 0.0
self.daily_stats = {}
self.notification_service = NotificationService()
self.analytics_service = AnalyticsService()
def add_order(self, order):
self.orders.append(order)
self.total_revenue += order.amount
self._update_daily_stats(order)
self._send_notifications(order)
self._track_analytics(order)
def _update_daily_stats(self, order):
date = order.created_at.date()
if date not in self.daily_stats:
self.daily_stats[date] = {"count": 0, "revenue": 0.0}
self.daily_stats[date]["count"] += 1
self.daily_stats[date]["revenue"] += order.amount
def _send_notifications(self, order):
if order.amount > 1000:
self.notification_service.send_high_value_alert(order)
if len(self.orders) % 100 == 0:
self.notification_service.send_milestone_alert(len(self.orders))
def _track_analytics(self, order):
self.analytics_service.track_order(order)
if self.total_revenue > 50000:
self.analytics_service.track_milestone("revenue_50k")
This looks reasonable at first glance. But let's visualize the hidden complexity:

A[add_order called] --> B[Update orders list]
B --> C[Update total_revenue]
C --> D[Update daily_stats]
D --> E[Send notifications]
E --> F[Track analytics]
G[❌ Miss one step?] --> H[Silent bugs]
I[❌ Add new derived state?] --> J[Update every entry point]
K[❌ Race condition?] --> L[Inconsistent state]

style K fill:#F44336,color:#fff
style H fill:#D32F2F,color:#fff
style J fill:#D32F2F,color:#fff
style L fill:#D32F2F,color:#fff
The Hidden Dependencies
The real problem isn't visible in the code - it's the implicit dependency graph:
graph LR
Orders[orders] --> Revenue[total_revenue]
Orders --> Stats[daily_stats]
Orders --> Notifications[notifications]
Orders --> Analytics[analytics]
Revenue --> Analytics
Stats --> Notifications
classDef implicit stroke-dasharray: 5 5
class Revenue,Stats,Notifications,Analytics implicit
These dependencies are
implicit
and
manually maintained
. Every time
orders
changes, you must remember to update all dependent values in the correct order.
1.
Tight Coupling Through Side Effects
Every time we add an order, we must remember to update:
Total revenue
Daily statistics
Notifications
Analytics
Any future derived state
Miss one update? Silent bugs. Add a new derived value? Modify every entry point.
2.
Implicit Dependencies
The relationship between orders and derived state is buried in imperative code. New developers (or future you) must trace through method calls to understand what depends on what.
3.
Inconsistent State Windows
Between the moment
orders.append(order)
executes and
total_revenue += order.amount
completes, your system is in an inconsistent state. In concurrent environments, this creates race conditions.
4.
Testing Complexity
Testing requires mocking all the side effects, or carefully orchestrating partial updates. Want to test just the revenue calculation? Good luck isolating it.
5.
Performance Blind Spots
Every order addition triggers every derived calculation, even if only some values are actually needed. No easy way to optimize without restructuring.

本文还提供了在现有系统中逐步采用信号的方法、常见模式与反模式，以及性能和测试方面的考虑。最终，文章帮助开发者判断何时应采用响应式状态管理，何时则不必。

44269289.article_content:
The Hat, the Spectre and SAT Solvers
Sat, Jan 27, 2024
16-minute read
Introduction
In this blog post you are going to read about two things:
A new flashy discovery in mathematics: aperiodic tilings of the plane with a single monotile
SAT solvers. A family of not so well known algorithms in computer science
Hopefully by the end of the post you will know a fair amount about the hat, the turtle and the spectres and have another powerful tool under your belt, SAT solvers.
Thus, you can see this post either as an exercise in recreational mathematics or as an invitation to SAT solvers.
The post is organized as follows. We first introduce the Hat and state the main result. Then we define what SAT solvers are. In section 3 we describe how we use the solver in wasm and apply it to the problem of solving a Sudoku problem as a warm up exercise in the next section. In section 5 we explain Craig Kaplan’s idea of how to use SAT solvers to tile finite regions of the plane and apply it to the Hat. Section 6 introduces the Turtle, a second monotile capable of tiling the plane aperiodically. With all those constructions we build the Spectre, from deformations of Hats and Turtles, a true chiral aperiodic monotile. In the last section we explain how to use the
app
Code
You can find all the code discussed here in
GitHub
.
There is an app you can play along with at:
https://www.nhatcher.com/hats/
The sudoku solver mentioned below is deployed at:
https://www.nhatcher.com/hats/sudoku.html
A small app solving general SAT problems in the browser:
https://www.nhatcher.com/hats/sat.html
I used the fantastic
dplr
SAT Solver by
Shuji Narazaki
and adapted it to wasm in:
https://github.com/nhatcher/splr-wasm
1. The Hat: a shape perplexing the world
It is quite unusual that a discovery in mathematics is understandable by the general public, but 2023 witnessed precisely that.
In November of 2022 just as ChatGPT was going to take world by a storm,
David Smith
a retired printer technician and amateur mathematician found a shape:
Thats is able to
tile
the whole infinite plane in a non periodic way:
The announcement was made in a
paper
but you might have heard of it in any of your favorite channels like
veritasium
,
numberphile
,
quanta magazine
or even the
New York Times
.
The story of non periodic tilings of the plane is somewhat old and was popularized by Sir Roger Penrose and Martin Gadner in his famous Scientific American column on recreational mathematics. For example Penrose found
two tiles
(the dart and the kite) that were able to tile the plane in a non periodic way.
In this blog post I will write a bit about these new tilings of the plane and how to cover finite regions using an algorithm that not many people, even people in the industry, know: a SAT solver.
2. The SAT solver, an underappreciated tool.
A
SATisfiability solver
is a computer program that solves problems in boolean algebra. Say you have a number of variables
a
,
b
,
c
,
d
, … that can be either
true
or
false
. And then you have a series of statements regarding those variables, like:
If
a
is
true
then either
b
is
true
or
c
is
false
.
If
a
and
b
are both
true
if and only if
d
or
c
is false.
Solvers can deal with problems with a lot of variables. We will run some experiments in your browser with more than 60 thousand variables and millions of statements.
To be able to use the solver we first need to convert all of our logic statements in what is called a
conjunctive normal form
(CNF). We don’t really need to explain much in here because as it happens the statements that we will produce are exactly in this form already.
In
conjunctive normal form
we have a series of statements, called
clauses
, that all need to be true (those are the conjunction or AND blocks). Each clause is composed of an OR array of literals (variables and their negations). For example:
a or b or not c
a or d
not c or d
This is composed of 3 clauses and there are 4 variables (a, b, c , d).
There is a general constructive theorem called the
Tseitin transformation
that converts any problem in boolean logic to an equivalent in CNF.
As I said, in our case the problem will already be in CNF so we don’t need to bother about that. The next step will be to write the problem in a way a Solver can digest it. The standard way is to assign a positive to each variable. For instance
a -> 1
b -> 2
c -> 3
d -> 4
The each clause is an array:
a or b or not c <=> [1, 2, -3]
As a you can see a negative value means negation of the variable.
Once you feed the solver an array of arrays it returns an array like [1, -2, 3, -4] that means variable 1 and 3 are true and variables 2 and 4 are false. The solver might not find a solution and will return an error or might be able to prove that there is not a valid a solution and will return “UNSAT”.
3. A SAT Solver in wasm
There are a million SAT solvers out there but we will use
splr
that we can compile to
WASM
, fits into a 200kB file and runs in the
browser
.

data.title: Using computers more freely and safely (2023)
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了如何更自由、安全地使用计算机。作者Kartik Agaram提出几点建议，包括选择用户数量较少、更新频率低、易于修改并常被分支（fork）的软件。这类软件由于不常更新，更容易被分支维护，且修改不需要特殊工具，理想情况下个人也能轻松做出小调整。作者强调，不需要一次性实现所有建议，每个建议的效益是累加的，按所需努力和技能排序，逐步改进。软件的复杂性和成本增加使其变得不可靠和缓慢，因此应减少对大规模软件的依赖，考虑使用用户较少、更本地化的软件（如“情境软件”），以增强信任和效率。最终目标是推动远离垄断，改善软件环境。

不同观点：
• [rpdillon] 认为中心化的应用商店对业余开发者不友好，导致商店中以商业软件为主，这些软件通常以提取用户数据或金钱为目的。他以F-Droid为例，说明去中心化的软件发布方式更好。他还分享了自己远离大型科技公司（如Meta、Microsoft）的经历，并强调了自己培养的反向权利态度，即不依赖于大型科技公司的产品。他指出，很多软件和服务其实是可有可无的，而这些公司正变得越来越具剥削性。

• [GMoromisato] 对[rpdillon]的观点不完全认同，认为商业软件和非商业软件都有其价值，并强调任何事物都有利弊，使用与否是权衡利弊后的选择。他批评了那些只谈论缺点而不提及优点的文章，认为这是一种片面的做法。他还提到，未来的理想情况可能是用户通过LLMs（大型语言模型）自行编写软件，以满足个性化需求。

补充讨论：
• [jay_kyburz] 对[rpdillon]的观点表示支持，简短地表达了对Lua语言的喜爱，可能暗示对简易编程和自定义软件的支持。

争议焦点：
• 中心化应用商店是否对业余开发者不友好，并导致软件生态的商业化和剥削性增强。
• 是否需要依赖大型科技公司提供的软件和服务，或者是否可以通过其他方式（如开源软件、自行编写软件）来替代。
• 对商业软件和非商业软件的权衡，以及在选择使用软件时应考虑哪些因素。

contact
Kartik Agaram
Freewheeling Apps
Using computers more freely and safely
Transcript for
this video
(18 minutes). Click on images for full-size versions.
How can we use computers more freely and safely?
the punchline
Prefer software:
with thousands rather than millions of users
that seldom requires updates
that spawns lots of forks
that is easy to modify
that
you
can modify
These are my suggestions.
Prefer software with thousands rather than millions of users,
that doesn't change often,
that seems to get forked a lot,
that can be modified without specialized tools, and, ideally
that you can make small changes to. Yourself. In a single
afternoon.
You don't have to do all this. Their benefits are additive, but acting
on even one of these suggestions is better than nothing. The suggestions
are arranged roughly in order of increasing effort and skill required.
Trying to follow one suggestion will pave the way for the others, should
you choose later to continue down this path. Software without constant
updates is easier for forks to keep up with. Forks are signs of
easily-modified software, and testimonials from nearby programmers can
be promising signs that, hey, maybe making a change yourself won't be
very hard.
The most important step is the first one. Humanity didn't get good at
building houses by building the same house a million times. We built
lots of different houses and learned from each other's failures.
Gravitating away from monopolies is a way everyone can help improve
software, regardless of our abilities or needs.
outline
Problems
Suggestions ↔ Examples
That's the whole argument in a nutshell. In the rest of this talk I want
to show how to apply these principles in small ways in your day-to-day
decision-making, making the world a little better in the process. I'll
show this by drawing on my own journey over the past year for examples.
I'll first back up to some problems I was responding to at the start,
then show how I responded fairly directly to these problems and ended up
with the above suggestions.
expensive
So, problems. The first problem is: software is expensive. We like to
think the incremental cost of software is 0. You build it once, lots of
people use it. The additional cost for any new user is negligible. This
is just not borne out by multiple decades of experience. Apps and
services require constant maintenance. And they grow complex over time,
so their costs grow over time.
untrustworthy
Also, software today is just not very trustworthy.
incompetence
Data breaches
impact millions of people every year
.
If you manage data for others it's extremely difficult to secure.
Efforts to secure it add to your costs.
malice
Beyond incompetence, services engage in rampant misbehavior.
This is a headline
from a couple of years ago. Just about every single major phone app was
snooping on your clipboard. And this was going on for years before these
researchers noticed.
Since they noticed, Apple plugged this loophole. But what else are apps
up to, and what current misbehavior will we find out about this year or
the next?
slow
Ok, so software providers fail to keep us secure and also do shady
stuff. What do we get for this? Are they at least effective at providing
the service they advertise?
Here is a talk
about how inefficient just about every single mainstream website is. Our
computers pay a tax on every page we read.
slow
But maybe that's just websites that have to go out over the internet.
What about native apps?
Here is a study
showing that a computer from 2015 is 2-5 times slower than an Apple 2e
from 1986 just at reading a keystroke and displaying it on screen.
all is not well with computers
they grow increasingly complex and expensive
they grow untrustworthy as they grow complex
they slow down as they grow complex
These are the fairly fundamental problems I see. They're not new or
insightful, lots of people have said all this. What do we do about it?
depend less on software
My first resolution is just to bring less software into my life. It is
still early days, we don't really understand computers yet. It's
important to be clear-eyed about the risks they bring with them, and to
think about computers primarily as a
liability
rather than an
asset.
depend on services with dozens of users
But, unfortunately, I came to this realization too late. Computers have
already eaten the world. Today I need to use computers to conduct
commerce, interact with my government, and to talk to my family and
friends. What to do about this?
One coping mechanism is an idea from almost 20 years ago called
situated software
.
This is software with a few users who know each other and share a social
context or
situation
. The idea is analogous to local
government: services with few stakeholders are often better able to meet
the needs of their stakeholders, particularly when everyone knows
everyone and there's a certain level of social accountability.

• [GMoromisato] 对[rpdillon]的观点不完全认同，认为商业软件和非商业软件都有其价值，并强调任何事物都有利弊，使用与否是权衡利弊后的选择。他批评了那些只谈论缺点而不提及优点的文章，认为这是一种片面的做法。他还提到，未来的理想情况可能是用户通过LLMs（大型语言模型）自行编写软件，以满足个性化需求。

补充讨论：
• [jay_kyburz] 对[rpdillon]的观点表示支持，简短地表达了对Lua语言的喜爱，可能暗示对简易编程和自定义软件的支持。

争议焦点：
• 中心化应用商店是否对业余开发者不友好，并导致软件生态的商业化和剥削性增强。
• 是否需要依赖大型科技公司提供的软件和服务，或者是否可以通过其他方式（如开源软件、自行编写软件）来替代。
• 对商业软件和非商业软件的权衡，以及在选择使用软件时应考虑哪些因素。

data.title: When random people give money to random other people (2017)
data.author: munificent
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了一个由Uri Wilensky提出的问题：在一个有100个人、每人有100美元的房间中，每人都随机选择另一个人并给其一美元。经过一段时间后，财富分布会如何变化？尽管人们可能预期财富会均匀分布，但模拟显示财富不均迅速出现并持续存在。

原因在于，这个随机过程实际上是在一个状态空间图上进行随机游走，该图的顶点代表所有可能的财富分配状态。尽管图并非完全规则，但在没有人破产的情况下，几乎每个节点的度数都是100。因此，长期来看，每个可能的状态几乎等概率出现，导致财富分布不均。

进一步分析表明，最富有者的预期财富大约为100倍的对数函数。当每人初始只有一美元时，财富分布更加不均，因为几乎肯定会有人破产。

这个问题类似于物理学中的玻尔兹曼分布计算，揭示了随机过程如何导致财富不平等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过一个模拟实验探讨随机性和财富不平等的关系，以及可能的解决方案和数学模型的准确性。

不同观点：
• Noelia- 认为随机性和时间可以自发导致财富不平等，不平等不一定源自不当行为。该现象引发了对如何应对不平等的思考。
• NooneAtAll3 对模型的数学部分提出质疑，指出游戏图节点的出度计算可能有误，并认为模型对稳态分布的假设缺乏依据。
• k__ 认为财富不平等的出现和持续是公平的，因为个人的财富在动态变化中。
• dgan 提出如果富人专门给钱给最穷的人，而不是随机分配，是否会更公平的问题。
• thaumasiotes 对模型中初始财富的设定提出质疑，并指出文章中关于状态概率的描述有误。
• wordglyph 建议引入信用机制，让没有钱的人也能参与分配，认为这样可能使财富更均匀。
• deadbabe 提议将该模型开发成一个加密货币游戏，玩家定期随机转账，并在固定时间后重新开始，以探索财富动态。
• MichaelRo 将随机财富分配比作税收和福利制度，认为这是一种维持公平的方式。

补充讨论：
• 模拟和数学模型的准确性是一个争议焦点，特别是NooneAtAll3和thaumasiotes对模型细节的质疑。
• 关于如何在模型中实现更公平的财富分配，dgan和wordglyph提出了不同的改进建议。
• 有人提议将该模型游戏化（deadbabe）或与现实中的经济政策联系起来（MichaelRo），以探索其实际应用。

总体来看，讨论围绕财富不平等的成因、模型的数学准确性以及可能的解决方案展开。不同的观点既有对模型的技术性质疑，也有对不平等现象的哲学思考和实际应用的建议。

44270144.article_content:
A post on Decision Science
about a problem of
Uri Wilensky
‘s has been making the rounds:
Imagine a room full of 100 people with 100 dollars each. With every tick of the clock, every person with money gives a dollar to one randomly chosen other person. After some time progresses, how will the money be distributed?
People often expect the distribution to be close to uniform.  But this isn’t right; the simulations in the post show clearly that inequality of wealth rapidly appears and then persists (though each individual person bobs up and down from rich to poor.)  What’s going on?  Why would this utterly fair and random process generate winners and losers?
Here’s one way to think about it.  The possible states of the system are the sets of nonnegative integers (m_1, .. m_100) summing to 10,000; if you like, the lattice points inside a simplex.  (From now on, let’s write N for 100 because who cares if it’s 100?)
The process is a random walk on a graph G, whose vertices are these states and where two vertices are connected if you can get from one to the other by taking a dollar from one person and giving it to another.  We are asking:  when you run the random walk for a long time, where are you on this graph?  Well, we know what the stationary distribution for random walk on an undirected graph is; it gives each vertex a probability proportional to its degree.  On a regular graph, you get uniform distribution.
Our state graph G isn’t regular, but it almost is; most nodes have degree N, where by “most” I mean “about 1-1/e”; since the number of states is
and, of these, the ones with degree N are exactly those in which nobody’s out of money; if each person has a dollar, the number of ways to distribute the remaining N^2 – N dollars is
and so the proportion of states where someone’s out of money is about
.
So, apart from those states where somebody’s broke, in the long run
every possible state is equally likely;
we are just as likely to see $9,901 in one person’s hands and everybody else with $1 as we are to see exact equidistribution again.
What is a random lattice point in this simplex like?  Good question!  An argument just like the one above shows that the probability nobody goes below $c is on order e^-c, at least when c is small relative to N; in other words, it’s highly likely that somebody’s very nearly out of money.
If X is the maximal amount of money held by any player, what’s the distribution of X?  I didn’t immediately see how to figure this out.  You might consider the continuous version, where you pick a point at random from the
real
simplex
.
Equivalently; break a stick at N-1 randomly chosen points; what is the length of the longest piece?
This is a well-studied problem
; the mean size of the longest piece is about N log N.  So I guess I think maybe that’s the expected value of the net worth of the richest player?
But it’s not obvious to me whether you can safely approximate the finite problem by its continuous limit (which corresponds to the case where we keep the number of players at N but reduce the step size so that each player can give each other a cent, or a picocent, or whatever.)
What happens if you give each of the N players just one dollar?  Now the uniformity really breaks down, because it’s incredibly unlikely that nobody’s broke.  The probability distribution on the set of (m_1, .. m_N) summing to N assigns each vector a probability proportional to the size of its support (i.e. the number of m_i that are nonzero.)  That must be a well-known distribution, right?  What does the corresponding distribution on partitions of N look like?
Update
:  Kenny Easwaran points out that this is basically the same computation physicists do
when they compute the Boltzmann distribution
, which was new to me.

data.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
data.author: archon1410
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为SEAL（Self-Adapting Language Models）的框架，使大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过生成自己的微调数据和更新指令进行自我适应。SEAL模型在接收到新输入时，会生成自编辑内容，这些内容可以重构信息、指定优化超参数或调用工具进行数据增强和基于梯度的更新。通过监督微调（SFT），这些自编辑会导致持久的权重更新，实现持续适应。为了训练模型生成有效的自编辑，文章使用了一个以更新后模型的下游性能作为奖励信号的强化学习循环。实验表明，SEAL在知识整合和少样本泛化方面表现出色，是语言模型自我导向适应的有前景的一步。相关代码和网站已提供。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）的自适应学习能力及其实用性

不同观点：
• **perrygeo**：LLMs缺乏像人类一样的持续学习能力，它们的训练和推理过程是分离的。这种静态特性导致人们误以为AGI（通用人工智能）即将到来，但实际上LLMs在推理结束后就停止了学习。
• **gavinray**：提到NEAT/HyperNEAT算法，这种算法通过演化网络拓扑来优化学习，与LLMs通过调整权重来学习的做法形成对比。他的两位从事ML早期的朋友坚信强化学习（RL）和演化算法是ML的未来方向。
• **xianshou**：赞赏自我编辑方法通过RL优化模型重构信息的能力，指出该方法可以发现更好的训练格式，但仍存在灾难性遗忘问题和高计算开销。他认为该方法适用于高价值文档处理，但限制于需要明确评估指标的任务。
• **libraryofbabel**：对LLMs在实际应用中“边做边学”的能力表示关注，质疑为何当前研究不更多关注这一方向，并指出这可能是实现AGI的关键障碍。

补充讨论：
• **cma**：提到Anthropic最近关于自我微调的研究，提供了一个相关的文献链接。
• **neuroelectron**：幽默地提到模型在实际应用中被限制为只读模式，类似于科幻电影中的情节。
• **all2**：提供了一个包含代码和示例的网站链接。
• **khalic**：引用研究预测到2028年LLMs将用尽所有公开的文本数据，指出合成数据增强的重要性，并建议通过元训练一个专门的SEAL合成数据生成器模型来解决数据墙问题。
• **Centigonal**：提出“正确遗忘”问题比“正确学习”问题更迫切，指出当前模型在遗忘不相关信息方面的能力不足。
• **b0a04gl**：质疑自我编辑模型的调试难度，担心如何确定错误输出是源于基础模型还是模型的自我编辑，并进一步讨论优化器行为监控的必要性。
• **yahoozoo**：质疑SEAL方法的创新性，认为其仅是利用HuggingFace库进行LoRA适配器的合并。
• **mackenziebowes**：对SEAL命名表示不满，认为SAL更为合适。
• **bravesoul2**：简单提到正接近重大突破。
• **ivape**：指出持续微调在云端LLMs上的可行性问题，认为当前硬件条件尚不支持这一设想。

争议焦点：
• LLMs的持续学习能力及其实际应用的可行性。
• 自我编辑方法的创新性和实用性。
• 调试和监控自我学习模型的难度。
• 数据墙问题及合成数据增强的潜在解决方案。

Title:
Self-Adapting Language Models
Authors:
Adam Zweiger
,
Jyothish Pari
,
Han Guo
,
Ekin Akyürek
,
Yoon Kim
,
Pulkit Agrawal
View a PDF of the paper titled Self-Adapting Language Models, by Adam Zweiger and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are powerful but static; they lack mechanisms to adapt their weights in response to new tasks, knowledge, or examples. We introduce Self-Adapting LLMs (SEAL), a framework that enables LLMs to self-adapt by generating their own finetuning data and update directives. Given a new input, the model produces a self-edit-a generation that may restructure the information in different ways, specify optimization hyperparameters, or invoke tools for data augmentation and gradient-based updates. Through supervised finetuning (SFT), these self-edits result in persistent weight updates, enabling lasting adaptation. To train the model to produce effective self-edits, we use a reinforcement learning loop with the downstream performance of the updated model as the reward signal. Unlike prior approaches that rely on separate adaptation modules or auxiliary networks, SEAL directly uses the model's own generation to control its adaptation process. Experiments on knowledge incorporation and few-shot generalization show that SEAL is a promising step toward language models capable of self-directed adaptation. Our website and code is available at

• **Centigonal**：提出“正确遗忘”问题比“正确学习”问题更迫切，指出当前模型在遗忘不相关信息方面的能力不足。
• **b0a04gl**：质疑自我编辑模型的调试难度，担心如何确定错误输出是源于基础模型还是模型的自我编辑，并进一步讨论优化器行为监控的必要性。
• **yahoozoo**：质疑SEAL方法的创新性，认为其仅是利用HuggingFace库进行LoRA适配器的合并。
• **mackenziebowes**：对SEAL命名表示不满，认为SAL更为合适。
• **bravesoul2**：简单提到正接近重大突破。
• **ivape**：指出持续微调在云端LLMs上的可行性问题，认为当前硬件条件尚不支持这一设想。

争议焦点：
• LLMs的持续学习能力及其实际应用的可行性。
• 自我编辑方法的创新性和实用性。
• 调试和监控自我学习模型的难度。
• 数据墙问题及合成数据增强的潜在解决方案。

data.title: MUMPS
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
MUMPS（Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System），又称M，是一种无类型、面向过程的编程语言，具有集成的事务处理键-值数据库。它由Neil Pappalardo、Robert A. Greenes和Curt Marble于1966-1967年在波士顿麻省总医院（MGH）开发，最初用于管理病人医疗记录和医院实验室信息系统。MUMPS后来成为美国健康信息系统和电子健康记录的主流数据库技术，如Epic Systems使用MUMPS为超过78%的美国患者提供服务。

MUMPS起源于对使用汇编语言开发医院信息系统的不满，其设计目标包括跨平台可移植性和多任务处理。该语言早期在PDP-7和PDP-9上运行，后来移植到多种系统如PDP-8、PDP-11等。MUMPS因其独特的集成数据库语言和高效的磁盘读写能力而广受医疗界欢迎。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MUMPS编程语言的特性、历史、实际使用体验及其在现代的应用和挑战

不同观点：
• skissane认为MUMPS的核心思想——内置持久化键值存储的语言——实际上很酷。尽管其经典实现存在很多缺陷，但这些缺陷在当时的资源限制下是有帮助的。现代实现已经使许多缺陷成为可选项，但许多主要代码库仍然使用极其简洁的遗留编码风格，这不利于可读性和维护。
• robertclaus则强调了MUMPS在实际使用中的独特体验，认为它更像是一个自定义操作系统而非编程语言。其代码与数据存储在一起，更改实时应用，并且难以与其他标准编程工具结合使用。
• telecomhacker作为兼职MUMPS程序员，表达了对该语言的喜爱，尤其是其高薪资待遇。他还提到MUMPS在美国的广泛使用使其成为一种“爱国语言”。

补充讨论：
• EvanAnderson和dang提供了外部链接，以更深入地了解MUMPS的实际应用及其引发的讨论。
• zeruch和JohnDeHope分享了他们学习或使用MUMPS的个人经历，认为这是一种有趣但非常奇怪的语言。
• royalwiggins指出了MUMPS在现代技术（如Caché Server Pages）中的应用。
• kiernanmcgowan和jaybrendansmith则关注MUMPS程序员的后续职业发展和他们的一些趣闻轶事。
• lowmagnet和paxys提到了与MUMPS相关的历史转换和技术挑战。
• mandevil和hellojesus推测了这个讨论主题突然出现的原因，可能与某些技术社区的活动或视频分享有关。
• clabretro分享了一个关于MUMPS的实用视频链接，为新手提供了直观的教程。

争议焦点：
• MUMPS的遗留编码风格与现代编码风格的冲突，以及为何没有更多地迁移到现代风格。
• MUMPS的独特特性和使用体验，使其在现代编程环境中显得格外不同，尤其是在与其他工具的兼容性方面。

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Programming language
This article is about the programming language. For the disease, see
Mumps
. For other uses, see
Mumps (disambiguation)
.
MUMPS
Paradigm
Imperative
,
procedural
Designed by
Neil Pappalardo
,  Curt Marble,
Robert A. Greenes
First appeared
1966
; 59 years ago
(
1966
)
Stable release
ANSI X11.1-1995
/    December 8, 1995
(
1995-12-08
)
Typing discipline
Typeless
OS
Cross-platform
Influenced by
JOSS
Influenced
PSL
,
Caché ObjectScript
,
GT.M
MUMPS
("Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System"), or
M
, is an imperative, high-level
programming language
with an integrated transaction processing
key–value database
.  It was originally developed at
Massachusetts General Hospital
for managing patient medical records and hospital laboratory information systems.
MUMPS technology has since expanded as the predominant database for health information systems and
electronic health records
in the United States.  MUMPS-based information systems, such as
Epic Systems
', provide health information services for over 78% of patients across the U.S.
[
1
]
A unique feature of the MUMPS technology is its integrated
database language
, allowing direct, high-speed read-write access to permanent disk storage.
[
2
]
History
[
edit
]
1960s-1970s - Genesis
[
edit
]
MUMPS was developed by
Neil Pappalardo
,
Robert A. Greenes
, and Curt Marble in Dr. Octo Barnett's lab at the
Massachusetts General Hospital
(MGH) in
Boston
during 1966 and 1967.
[
3
]
It grew out of frustration, during a
National Institutes of Health
(NIH) supported hospital information systems project at the MGH, with the development in assembly language on a time-shared
PDP-1
by primary contractor
Bolt, Beranek & Newman
(BBN).  MUMPS came out of an internal "
skunkworks
" project at MGH by Pappalardo, Greenes, and Marble to create an alternative development environment. As a result of initial demonstration of capabilities, Dr. Barnett's proposal to NIH in 1967 for renewal of the hospital computer project grant took the bold step of proposing that the system be built in MUMPS going forward, rather than relying on the BBN approach. The project was funded, and serious implementation of the system in MUMPS began.
The original MUMPS system was, like
Unix
a few years later, built on a
DEC
PDP-7
. Octo Barnett and Neil Pappalardo obtained a
backward compatible
PDP-9
, and began using MUMPS in the admissions cycle and laboratory test reporting. MUMPS was then an
interpreted language
, yet even then, it incorporated a
hierarchical database
file system to standardize interaction with the data and abstract disk operations so they were only done by the MUMPS language itself. MUMPS was also used in its earliest days in an experimental clinical progress note entry system
[
4
]
and a radiology report entry system.
[
5
]
Some aspects of MUMPS can be traced from
RAND Corporation
's
JOSS
through
BBN
's
TELCOMP
and
STRINGCOMP
.  The MUMPS team chose to include portability between machines as a design goal.
An advanced feature of the MUMPS language not widely supported in
operating systems
or in
computer hardware
of the era was
multitasking
. Although
time-sharing
on
mainframe computers
was increasingly common in systems such as
Multics
, most mini-computers did not run parallel programs and threading was not available at all. Even on mainframes, the variant of batch processing where a program was run to completion was the most common implementation for an operating system of multi-programming.
It was a few years until Unix was developed. The lack of memory management hardware also meant that all multi-processing was fraught with the possibility that a memory pointer could change some other process. MUMPS programs do not have a standard way to refer to memory directly at all, in contrast to
C language
, so since the multitasking was enforced by the language, not by any program written in the language it was impossible to have the risk that existed for other systems.
Dan Brevik's DEC MUMPS-15 system was adapted to a DEC
PDP-15
, where it lived for some time. It was first installed at Health Data Management Systems of Denver in May 1971.
[
6
]
The portability proved to be useful and MUMPS was awarded a government research grant, and so MUMPS was released to the public domain which was a requirement for grants. MUMPS was soon ported to a number of other systems including the popular DEC
PDP-8
, the
Data General Nova
and on DEC
PDP-11
and the
Artronix
PC12 minicomputer
. Word about MUMPS spread mostly through the medical community, and was in widespread use, often being locally modified for their own needs.
Versions of the MUMPS system were rewritten by technical leaders Dennis "Dan" Brevik and Paul Stylos
[
6
]
of
DEC
in 1970 and 1971. By the early 1970s, there were many and varied implementations of MUMPS on a range of hardware platforms. Another noteworthy platform was Paul Stylos'
[
6
]
DEC MUMPS-11 on the PDP-11,

data.title: Thiings
data.author: pentagrama
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了如何在找不到所需物品时进行操作。如果用户在收藏中找不到特定物品，可以申请请求该物品。文章提供了一个链接，用户可以通过点击"Request a Thiing"来提交他们的请求。这一功能方便用户获取未包含在当前收藏中的所需物品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Thiings网站及其内容、功能、版权和实用性的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• [paxys] 质疑网站声称的"免费"性质，因为下载整个图标集合需要付费。同时，对内容许可协议表示困惑，指出网站声称任何人都可以下载和使用图标，但未明确说明具体的许可类型。
• [huhtenberg] 提到另一个类似的但更全面的网站——The Noun Project，暗示Thiings的独特性和实用性可能不如竞争对手。
• [dvh] 对网站的搜索功能提出批评，指出搜索结果不准确，例如搜索“asp”时没有相关选项，却出现了“wasp”。
• [timnetworks] 指出网站在音频播放方面存在加载时间问题，导致音频播放时可能不完整。
• [fredley] 指出网站上伦敦桥的图片有误，实际展示的是塔桥，反映了内容准确性的问题。
• [toddmorey] 对如何生成具有风格一致性的自定义图标表示兴趣，寻求资源和建议。
• [wvbdmp] 对网站包含军事内容如“Reaper Drone”和“坦克”，但没有某些日常生活物品如“dildo”表示不解。

补充讨论：
• [_august] 提供了一个相关的GitHub项目链接，用于生成Genmoji风格的图像，扩展了讨论的范围。
• [awfulneutral] 对网站上恐龙图像的科学准确性提出批评，特别是与《侏罗纪公园》相关的图像。
• [Waterluvian] 认为网站在手机上的导航体验不佳，但认为其设计接近令人愉快，提出了改进建议。
• [HanClinto] 对网站的存在目的和持续性表示怀疑，并对网站的版权语言和商业模式提出疑问，指出其未使用明确的CC-BY-NC等许可协议。
• [the-anarchist] 对如何保存图案和调整背景颜色提出技术性问题，寻求解决方案。
• [Centigonal] 认为网站的商业模式难以在市场竞争中长期生存，指出图标市场竞争激烈且成本低。
• [kurrupttt] 对网站的内容表示满意，认为其提供的3D元素对个人项目非常有用，持积极态度。
• [ipsum2] 认为网站的AI生成图标质量较高，但没有明确的使用场景。

争议焦点：
• 网站内容的免费与付费下载之间的矛盾以及内容许可的不明确性是主要的争议点。
• 网站内容的科学准确性和搜索功能的准确性也引发了用户的批评。
• 网站的商业模式和长期生存能力受到质疑。

总结：用户对Thiings网站的图标质量和创意表示了一定的认可，但在内容许可、功能实现和商业模式等方面提出了较多质疑和改进建议。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ReFLeCT成像技术的特点和创新

不同观点：
• **[reptation]** 通过分享多个视频链接，暗示或提供实际的成像结果来展示技术的实际应用。虽然没有明确的文字评论，但通过提供视觉材料，支持该技术在多毫米三维视野中捕捉整个断层扫描的能力。

• **[JPLeRouzic]** 引用技术文献，强调ReFLeCT能够以每秒120个体积的速度同步捕捉多个不受约束、未麻醉的模式生物的整个断层扫描。这个评论集中于技术的定量性能指标，如速度和视野范围，支持该技术在高速度和大视野成像中的优势。

• **[gsf_emergency_2]** 指出该技术的设计关键在于使用了一个反射凹面镜，这是其他 Fourier X 领域的研究者没有采用的方法。这表明该技术在设计上的创新性和独特性，强调其在领域内的技术突破。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点可能在于该技术的实际应用效果和相对于其他技术的显著优势。虽然提供了数据和视频链接，但具体的比较和应用实例讨论较少。

• 讨论中提到了技术的核心设计元素——反射凹面镜，这可能是技术创新的核心，但具体的实现细节和相对于其他技术的优越性仍需进一步探讨。

• 总体来看，讨论主要围绕ReFLeCT技术的速度、视野范围和设计独特性展开，支持者通过引用文献和提供视频材料来证明其优势。

data.title: Student discovers fungus predicted by Albert Hoffman
data.author: zafka
data.article_summary: 西弗吉尼亚大学（WVU）环境微生物学专业的学生Corinne Hazel发现了一种新的真菌物种，这种真菌可能用于治疗多种医疗疾病。她在研究牵牛花如何通过根部分泌麦角生物碱时，发现了一种名为*Periglandula clandestina*的新真菌，这种真菌能够产生与LSD类似的效果。她的发现是在与植物与土壤科学教授Daniel Panaccione合作下完成的，并得到了WVU Davis学院学生增强基金的资助。基因测序确认了这一新物种，其基因序列现已存入基因库。这种真菌能高效生产麦角生物碱，可能在未来药物开发中发挥重要作用。Hazel目前正在研究如何最佳地培养这种生长缓慢的真菌，并探索其他牵牛花物种是否也含有未被描述的真菌共生体。这一发现为医药和农业研究开辟了新的方向。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕LSD、其来源、用途以及相关科学发现的讨论，包括历史背景、科学贡献以及现代研究进展。

不同观点：
• driggs：指出霍夫曼（Albert Hofmann）在研究麦角生物碱及LSD时，并未知晓植物与真菌的共生关系。其他研究者曾质疑霍夫曼的样本受到污染，但最终其工作因植物内生真菌关系的揭示而得到证实。
• Zaylan：对学生发现霍夫曼近百年前怀疑的植物-真菌共生关系表示赞赏，并提出可能还有许多未被发现的隐藏化学过程在植物中悄然进行，暗示自然界中可能存在大量未开发的潜力。
• homeonthemtn：赞赏文章对迷幻化合物讨论时所持的成熟 tone。
• hollerith：引用YouTube视频内容，质疑LSD治疗PTSD的说法，提醒人们注意LSD可能带来的风险。
• doormatt：质疑基因组测序的“重大意义”，因为测序工作是由外部公司完成的，学生只是参与了送样过程。

• gwbas1c：质疑LSD用于治疗抑郁症、PTSD和成瘾症的合法性，指出LSD是附表1药物，通常不应有合法用途。
• throwing_away：询问是否可以获取克隆用于研究目的。
• scythe：指出临床上更多使用麦角生物碱的合成衍生物（如ergonovine）来治疗疾病，并提到培养麦角本身非常困难，因此对新真菌的培养尝试具有重要意义。
• zer00eyz：对文章中将LSD描述为用于治疗抑郁症、PTSD等疾病的用途表示怀疑，暗示LSD仍然是具有争议的物质。

WVU student discovers long-awaited mystery fungus sought by LSD’s inventor
Monday, June 02, 2025
Corinne Hazel, a WVU environmental microbiology major from Delaware, Ohio, has discovered a new species of fungus that may treat a variety of medical conditions.
(WVU Photo/Brian Persinger)
Download full-size
Making a discovery with the
potential for innovative applications in pharmaceutical development, a
West Virginia University
microbiology
student has found a long sought-after fungus that produces effects similar to the
semisynthetic drug LSD, which is used to treat conditions like depression,
post-traumatic stress disorder and addiction.
Corinne Hazel, of Delaware,
Ohio, an environmental microbiology major and
Goldwater
Scholar
, discovered the new species of fungus growing in morning
glory plants and named it Periglandula clandestina.
Hazel made the discovery
while working in the lab with
Daniel
Panaccione
, Davis-Michael Professor
of
Plant
and Soil Sciences
at the
WVU Davis College of Agriculture and
Natural Resources
. She
was studying how morning glories disperse protective chemicals called “ergot
alkaloids” through their roots when she saw evidence of a fungus.
“We had a ton of plants
lying around and they had these tiny little seed coats,” she said. “We noticed a
little bit of fuzz in the seed coat. That was our fungus.”
The researchers prepared a DNA sample
and sent it away for genome sequencing, funded by a
WVU Davis
College Student Enhancement Grant
obtained by Hazel. The sequencing confirmed
the discovery of a new species and the sequence is now deposited in a gene bank
with her name on it.
“Sequencing a genome is a significant
thing,” Panaccione said. “It’s amazing for a student.”
Morning glory plants live
in symbiosis with fungi that produce the same ergot alkaloids the Swiss chemist
Albert Hofmann modified when he invented LSD in the late 1930s.
Hofmann hypothesized that
a fungus in morning glories produced alkaloids similar to those in LSD, but the
species remained a mystery until Hazel and Panaccione’s discovery. They published their findings in
Mycologia
.
“Morning glories contain
high concentrations of similar lysergic acid derivatives that give them their
psychedelic activities,” Panaccione said. “This inspired Hofmann and others to
investigate morning glories for the presence of a hidden fungus related to the
ergot fungus that might be the source of these chemicals. They found very
similar chemicals, but they could never find the fungus itself.”
Ergot alkaloids are made
exclusively by fungi. In addition to morning glories, they’re often found
growing on grains like rye. They can be poisonous to humans and livestock and, when
used therapeutically, can have unwanted side effects. Still, some clinicians use
them to treat conditions like migraines, dementia, uterine hemorrhaging and
Parkinson’s disease.
Periglandula clandestina is highly
efficient at making ergot alkaloids in large quantities, a characteristic that may
play a role in future pharmaceuticals. The discovery of the fungus o
pens a host of potential research
avenues, Panaccione said.
“Many things are toxic. But if you
administer them in the right dosage or modify them, they can be useful
pharmaceuticals. By studying them, we may be able to figure out ways to bypass
the side effects. These are big issues for medicine and agriculture.”
The researchers dubbed the fungus “Periglandula
clandestina” for its ability to have eluded investigators for decades.
“I think that’s the perfect name,”
Panaccione said. “And I love that we did this project together. Corinne has a
ton of talent. It’s about students recognizing the opportunities, seizing them
and having the skill and the brain power to bring this work to fruition.”
Hazel is now studying the most
effective ways to culture the slow-growing fungus and is interested in whether other
morning glory species may also contain ergot alkaloids from a fungal symbiote
that has yet to be described.
“I’m lucky to have stumbled into this
opportunity,” she said. “People have been looking for this fungus for years,
and one day, I look in the right place, and there it is. I’m very proud of the
work that I’ve done at WVU.”
-WVU-

data.title: Simulink (Matlab) Copilot
data.author: kaamuli
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个名为Bloxi的项目，它是一个由帝国理工学院航空工程二年级学生开发的AI助手，能够将自然语言提示转换为可运行的Simulink控制系统模型，并进行实时调试。该项目利用OpenAI的API实现多模态功能，可以逐步生成和连接Simulink模块，并通过截图和LLM检查不一致之处。项目包含两个主要脚本和一个简单后端，用户只需输入自己的OpenAI API密钥即可使用。尽管最初只是个人项目，但随着MathWorks宣布开发类似工具，作者决定分享Bloxi，以供他人进一步开发和使用。项目遵循MIT许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Matlab和Simulink的使用及其与新兴AI工具的结合

不同观点：
• [支持Matlab/Simulink的观点] stochtastic认为，尽管在某些行业和学术领域Matlab不再流行，并且其许可和商业模式受到批评，但在某些领域，Matlab和Simulink仍然是无可比拟的工具。他认为对这些产品的负面评价往往是过度的，并鼓励继续使用适合工作的工具。

• [AI工具的优势与创新] kaamuli作为一名航空工程学生和全栈开发者，分享了自己开发的AI助手Bloxi，该工具利用LLM和“提示工程”技术，将自然语言转换为Simulink模型，并实时调试。他认为这种工具可以极大地提高工程学生的生产力，类似于程序员通过Copilot获得的效率提升。他还提到MathWorks正在开发类似版本，显示出这种创新具有实际应用价值。

补充讨论：
• [Bloxi的功能和实现] kaamuli详细介绍了Bloxi的工作原理，包括两个主要脚本和一个后端系统，用于构建Simulink模型和处理聊天及用户界面。他还提供了使用OpenAI API的步骤，并通过视频和GitHub链接展示了工具的实际应用和开源代码，供他人进一步开发和改进。

• [争议焦点] 评论中隐含的一个争议点是Matlab和Simulink的高效性和其商业模式的批评之间的矛盾。stochtastic认为对这些产品的负面评价往往是不公正的，而kaamuli的工具则展示了通过开源和AI技术解决传统工具使用中的痛点，可能暗示了对Matlab/Simulink某些局限性的改进需求。

• [创新与竞争] kaamuli提到MathWorks正在开发类似工具，显示出这种创新不仅仅是个人的兴趣项目，也得到了大公司的关注，可能引发更多关于知识产权和市场竞争的讨论。

整体来看，讨论围绕Matlab/Simulink在特定领域的不可替代性与AI工具带来的创新和效率提升之间的平衡展开。同时，开源工具Bloxi的分享也为工程教育和实践提供了新的可能性。

Before I start - Yes, I know the differential equation in the video is wrong. I’ve already fixed it by tweaking the prompt and the script so the inputs depend on what’s being asked. The original issue was that blocks like Sum were being pasted in without matching the right number of inputs and outputs.
I’m a 2nd-year aero-engineering student at Imperial College London, I enjoy problem solving (did BPhO - gold and UKMT Gold) I'm a full-stack dev (or atleast trying to be lol) who hacked together Bloxi, an AI copilot that sits on top of Simulink and turns plain-English prompts into working control-system models and can easily debug them in real time. I felt the pain myself this term, watching top-tier students burn hours wiring blocks instead of engineering. With today’s multimodal LLMs finally able to “see” diagrams, this is the first moment an assistant like Bloxi can exist and the fastest way to give millions of engineers the same productivity leap coders just got.I built this mainly to get comfortable with LLMs and “prompt-engineering,” and I think I’ve hit the point where I’m done tinkering—especially now that MathWorks have announced they’re working on their own version. So I figured I’d share what I’ve got in case anyone wants to take it further and also just to like give it out to the world innit.
How it works:
Two scripts + simple backend (3):
One builds the Simulink model.
The other handles the chat + simple UI.
Backend that glues together the OpenAI API and frontend
Drop in your own OpenAI API key and you’re off. I used it to debug and build a few uni-project models, and it’s been surprisingly handy.
At first it just spat out a finished Simulink file, but I wanted that ChatGPT “walk-through” vibe make it feel 'magical'. So I added a couple of for loops: one to drop in blocks step-by-step, and another to wire them up.
Since raw code isn’t visible in Simulink (to the best of my knowledge), within one of my scripts I had it walk through the simulink file and screenshot each stage leveraging the fact openAI's API is multimodal, pipe them through the LLM, and let it spot inconsistencies. Works better than I expected. Perhaps someone can do better or find a better way?
Youtube video of me using it is
https://youtu.be/TX0fviaFSyg
To use download & open scripts then just do openChatbox().

Research
Strange radio pulses detected coming from ice in Antarctica
The unusual radio pulses were detected by the Antarctic Impulsive Transient Antenna (ANITA) experiment, a range of instruments flown on balloons high above Antarctica that are designed to detect radio waves from cosmic rays hitting the atmosphere.
Credit:
Stephanie Wissel / Penn State
.
Creative Commons
Expand
June 13, 2025
By
Marina Naumova
UNIVERSITY PARK, Pa. — A cosmic particle detector in Antarctica has emitted a series of bizarre signals that defy the current understanding of particle physics, according to an international research group that includes scientists from Penn State. The unusual radio pulses were detected by the Antarctic Impulsive Transient Antenna (ANITA) experiment, a range of instruments flown on balloons high above Antarctica that are designed to detect radio waves from cosmic rays hitting the atmosphere.
The goal of the experiment is to gain insight into distant cosmic events by analyzing signals that reach the Earth.  Rather than reflecting off the ice, the signals — a form of radio waves — appeared to be coming from below the horizon, an orientation that cannot be explained by the current understanding of particle physics and may hint at new types of particles or interactions previously unknown to science, the team said.
The researchers published their results in the journal
Physical Review Letters
.
“The radio waves that we detected were at really steep angles, like 30 degrees below the surface of the ice,” said Stephanie Wissel, associate professor of physics, astronomy and astrophysics who worked on the ANITA team searching for signals from elusive particles called neutrinos.
She explained that by their calculations, the anomalous signal had to pass through and interact with thousands of kilometers of rock before reaching the detector, which should have left the radio signal undetectable because it would have been absorbed into the rock.
“It’s an interesting problem because we still don't actually have an explanation for what those anomalies are, but what we do know is that they're most likely not representing neutrinos,” Wissel said.
Neutrinos, a type of particle with no charge and the smallest mass of all subatomic particles, are abundant in the universe. Usually emitted by high-energy sources like the sun or major cosmic events like supernovas or even the Big Bang, there are neutrino signals everywhere. The problem with these particles, though, is that they are notoriously difficult to detect, Wissel explained.
“You have a billion neutrinos passing through your thumbnail at any moment, but neutrinos don't really interact,” she said. “So, this is the double-edged sword problem. If we detect them, it means they have traveled all this way without interacting with anything else. We could be detecting a neutrino coming from the edge of the observable universe.”
Once detected and traced to their source, these particles can reveal more about cosmic events than even the most high-powered telescopes, Wissel added, as the particles can travel undisturbed and almost as fast as the speed of light, giving clues about cosmic events that happened lightyears away.
Wissel and teams of researchers around the world have been working to design and build special detectors to capture sensitive neutrino signals, even in relatively small amounts. Even one small signal from a neutrino holds a treasure trove of information, so all data has significance, she said.
“We use radio detectors to try to build really, really large neutrino telescopes so that we can go after a pretty low expected event rate,” said Wissel, who has designed experiments to spot neutrinos in Antarctica and South America.
ANITA is one of these detectors, and it was placed in Antarctica because there is little chance of interference from other signals. To capture the emission signals, the balloon-borne radio detector is sent to fly over stretches of ice, capturing what are called ice showers.
“We have these radio antennas on a balloon that flies 40 kilometers above the ice in Antarctica,” Wissel said. “We point our antennas down at the ice and look for neutrinos that interact in the ice, producing radio emissions that we can then sense on our detectors.”
These special ice-interacting neutrinos, called tau neutrinos, produce a secondary particle called a tau lepton that is released out of the ice and decays, the physics term referring to how the particle loses energy as it travels over space and breaks down into its constituents. This produces emissions known as air showers.
If they were visible to the naked eye, air showers might look like a sparkler waved in one direction, with sparks trailing it, Wissel explained. The researchers can distinguish between the two signals — ice and air showers — to determine attributes about the particle that created the signal.

Austin Z. Henley

Carnegie Mellon University
azhenley@cmu.edu
@austinzhenley
github/AZHenley

Publications

The fastest way to detect a vowel in a string
6/13/2025
See the discussion of this post on
Hacker News
.
I was nerdsniped recently:
What is the best way to detect if a string has a vowel in it?
This is trivial, right?
But as I started getting into it, I realized there is much more to this. I challenged myself to come up with as many ways to detect a vowel as possible. I even asked a few friends to give it a go. Which is the fastest? Which should never be used? Which is the most clever? Which is the most readable?
This post involves 11 different methods of detecting a vowel, algorithmic analysis, dissembling Python bytecode, inspecting the CPython implementation, and even looking at compiled regex opcodes. Let's go.
def has_vowels(s: str) -> bool:
...
This is the function stub I'm filling in. If there is at least one vowel in the input string, return True, otherwise return False. You can find the code from this post on
GitHub
.
Method #1: For loop
I started with the naive approach:
def loop_in(s):
for c in s.lower():
if c in "aeiou":
return True
return False
This is reasonable, readable, and probably without performance issues.
Except it does bother me that we are calling
lower()
which will always create a copy (appending to a string will
sometimes
mutate it in place but lower does
not
). We can fix it easily:
def loop_in(s):
for c in s:
if c in "aeiouAEIOU":
return True
return False
Method #2: For loop, C-style
A less Pythonic variation of our for loop:
def loop_or(s):
for c in s.lower():
if c == 'a' or c == 'e' or c == 'i' or c == 'o' or c == 'u':
return True
return False
Method #3: Nested for loop
And if we want to be exhaustive, then we should try a nested for loop:
def nested_loop(s):
vowels = "aeiouAEIOU"
for c in s:
for v in vowels:
if c == v:
return True
return False
Method #4: Set intersection
Time to get interesting. Here is my favorite solution that I thought of:
def set_intersection(s):
return set(s) & set("aeiouAEIOU")
It is short, clean, and a little bit clever.
Put the input string into a set, put the vowels into another set, and do set intersection. Sets are quite efficient. Inserting into the first set is
O(n)
, the second set is constant length so creating it is
O(1)
, and the set intersection is proportional to the smaller of the two sets, which is constant length, so
O(1)
, for a overall time complexity of
O(n)
.
However, it will process the entire input string rather than terminate at the first vowel. For really long strings where vowels show up early, it will do a lot of useless work.
Method #5: Generator Expression
def any_gen(s):
return any(c in "aeiouAEIOU" for c in s)
People love one liners. I channeled my inner Pythonista and came up with a generator expression like this. I think the performance will be equivalent to the first method, plus a bit of overhead for the generator object.
Method #6: Recursion
Now that I'm getting into the functional headspace, we have to try recursion:
def recursion(s):
if not s:
return False
return s[0] in "aeiouAEIOU" or recursion(s[1:])
CPython won't bode well with this. It will create a new string for every character in the input string, and it will crash if the string length is 1000 (max recursion limit).
Method #7: Regex search
Whenever strings are involved, someone will say to use regex.
import re
def regex(s):
return bool(re.search(r'[aeiouAEIOU]', s))
In the best case, I expect this to have performance similar to the C-style loop with some additional overhead to initialize.
Method #8: Regex replace
import re
def regex_replace(s):
return len(re.sub(r'[aeiouAEIOU]', '', s)) != len(s)
This will replace all vowels and then compare the string lengths to see if any were removed. It is inefficient because it won't short circuit and it creates a copy of the string.
Method #9: Filter
Now that we have the obvious approaches, what else can we do?
def filter_lambda(s):
return bool(list(filter(lambda x: x in "aeiouAEIOU", s)))
It works but it is wasteful and won't terminate early.
Method #10: Map
Similar but perhaps a bit better:
def map_lambda(s):
return any(map(lambda x: x in "aeiouAEIOU", s))
Using lambdas does increase your coolness, but is this an improvement over what we have so far? The book
Effective Python
says,
"list comprehensions are clearer than the map and filter built-in functions because they don't require lambda expressions"
. So it is less readable and likely less efficient than some of the other methods.
Method #11: Prime numbers
One of my former students,
Gregory Croisdale
, came up with an off-the-wall creative approach:
primes = [i for i in range(2, 1000) if factorial(i - 1) % i == (i - 1)]

vowels = "aeiouAEIOU"
vowel_primes_dict = {c: primes[ord(c)] for c in vowels}
try:
s_num = reduce(lambda acc, v: acc * primes[ord(v)], s, 1)
v_num = reduce(lambda acc

• Quantum_state强调，LLM本质上是概率数学函数，其输出必须经过人类智能的过滤才能被认真对待。
• Havoc建议通过反向提问获取更有用的反馈，例如询问某个糟糕想法为何糟糕，以测试LLM的反馈一致性。

• Kypro抱怨LLM在与其意见不同时，表达方式往往显得居高临下，且倾向于诉诸权威或情感来反驳用户。
• Api指出，LLM也会批评用户，不仅仅是迎合。
• Photochemsyn对ChatGPT的奉承模块表示不满，认为其误导用户对良好提示结构的理解，并批评了投资者对LLM的过度追逐，主张工具应开放给所有人使用。

• LLM的使用方法：不同用户分享了如何更有效地使用LLM获取有用信息的方法，例如并行处理、反向提问和反复修正等。

data.title: Implementing Logic Programming
data.author: sirwhinesalot
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：逻辑编程的各种实现和应用

不同观点：
• [sundarurfriend] 认为 Brachylog 作为一种高尔夫语言，提供了非常愉悦的编程体验，尤其是在解决问题的过程中采用不同寻常的思维方式，但这种体验可能与用于实际编码的逻辑编程不同。
• [kragen] 推荐 miniKanren 和 microKanren，并认为通过实现 microKanren 可以获得极大的教育价值，同时指出 Datalog 更适合用于数据库的深入研究，而不是逻辑编程。
• [philzook] 提到了一种简单的 Datalog 实现，并展示了如何通过 SQL 风格的实现获得性能和功能上的提升，同时分享了一个从 Z3 AST 到 sqlite 的 Datalog 实现。
• [ashton314] 分享了自己实现 miniKanren 的详细过程，并提到实现了一个小型类型检查器，可以通过逆向运行生成符合给定类型的程序。
• [xelxebar] 推荐了一个用 Prolog 实现的窗口管理器，并表示通过使用该项目成功学习了 Prolog，同时寻求更多高质量逻辑编程代码库的阅读推荐。
• [deosjr] 分享了自己使用 miniKanren、Datalog 和 WebAssembly 实现 Bret Victor's Dynamicland 的经验，认为掌握小型逻辑编程语言的实现是一种强大的能力。
• [tracnar] 提到一个用 Soufflé 实现的逻辑编程项目，虽然觉得很有趣，但还没有找到实际应用的借口。
• [scapbi] 提到在 Mochi 项目中添加逻辑编程层的经验，利用 OpenAI Codex 生成了一个工作中的 Datalog 引擎，并提供了详细的实现过程和代码链接。
• [xlii] 分享了自己对 Prolog 实现和 Constraint Handling Rules 的研究，并提到了 CLIPS，认为这是一个很有前途的项目，特别是对于规则解析的快速支持和易于集成。
• [jpfr] 认为 miniKanren 等项目虽然不错，但正在形成一种单一文化，忽略了其他方法，并提到构建 Warren's Abstract Machine (WAM) 是 Prolog 实现的传统入门项目。
• [fracus] 认为应该从一个具体问题出发，描述逻辑编程如何比其他范式更好地解决该问题。
• [michae2] 对 Datalog 中添加整数和字符串的支持表示关注，担心这会影响查询评估的终止保证，并寻求解决方案。
• [IamDaedalus] 表示对 Prolog 的兴趣，并计划在周末尝试。
• [kriro] 对 Prolog 有深厚感情，但提到其实际使用中可能导致代码的“混乱”，并询问嵌入 Kanren 是否是推荐的做法，同时表达了对 Prolog 现状的兴趣。
• [usgroup] 认为 Prolog 似乎陷入了被遗忘和重新发现的循环。

补充讨论：
• 逻辑编程在不同项目和语言中的具体实现和应用，如 Brachylog、miniKanren、microKanren、Datalog 和 Prolog。
• 对 Datalog 中添加新功能（如整数和字符串）的技术挑战和解决方案的探讨。
• 逻辑编程在实际项目中的使用经验和教育价值，以及对高质量逻辑编程代码库的需求。
• Prolog 的历史和现状，以及其在开发者社区中的周期性兴趣。

data.title: Whatever Happened to Sandboxfs?
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何解决macOS上构建系统中的性能问题和隔离问题，尤其是在涉及缓存、内容可寻址存储（CAS）和沙盒机制时。

不同观点：
• [comex]: 提出macOS新加入的类似FUSE的API可能带来的性能问题，特别是在编译器因隔离机制无法访问缓存时，会导致构建速度变慢。comex认为理想的解决方案是让Bazel与LLVM的CAS集成，并提到通过实现Swift和Clang的“显式模块构建”可能会有所帮助。

• [ajb]: 认为使用NFS来解决沙盒问题是一个早就被Vesta构建系统在20年前采用的方法，对现代系统的“重新发现”这一结论表示惊讶。

• [o11c]: 建议在一定程度上信任工具二进制文件的前提下，使用类似`LD_PRELOAD`的方法来拦截系统调用如`open`等，以此解决某些隔离问题。同时提到使用Go语言可能会使这种方法变得复杂。o11c还提出是否可以保留符号链接森林而仅删除其他文件的设想。

• [dangoodmanUT]: 认为新的ASIF稀疏镜像格式和macOS Tahoe的新容器化框架可以解决大部分相关问题，暗示这些新技术可能会提供更好的解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术包括FUSE-like API、LLVM的CAS、NFS、`LD_PRELOAD`方法、Swift和Clang的模块构建、ASIF稀疏镜像格式以及macOS Tahoe的容器化框架。
• 争议焦点在于如何在保证隔离的前提下优化构建速度，特别是在涉及缓存和系统调用拦截时。不同的技术方案在讨论中被提出和比较。
• 不同观点之间存在对旧技术（如NFS）和新技术的评价差异，以及对各种技术实现细节的可行性讨论。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RISC-V指令集架构的发展速度与其他ISA（如Arm和x86）的比较

不同观点：
• justin66认为原文中的说法存在明显错误，特别是关于RISC-V自2014年推出以来以Arm和x86从未经历过的速度演变的描述。justin66指出，PC领域从8086到80486的演变仅用了11年，暗示x86的发展速度也非常快，不亚于RISC-V。

补充讨论：
• justin66通过具体例子（8086到80486的演变仅用11年）来反驳原文中RISC-V发展速度独一无二的观点，表明x86架构也有过快速发展的时期。
• 争议的焦点在于RISC-V的发展速度是否真的比Arm和x86更为迅速，以及如何衡量这种速度。justin66提出了历史比较，质疑原文中对RISC-V独特性的宣称。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EDAN工具的有效性和使用场景

不同观点：
• **支持观点（mikeytown2）**：EDAN工具能够快速、准确地评估程序是否受益于更快的内存或额外的缓存。通过一次普通的程序运行和一些智能分析，用户可以明确了解延迟在哪些地方重要，哪些地方不重要。这一观点强调了EDAN的效率和实用性，尤其是在优化程序性能时提供的清晰指导。

补充讨论：
• 该评论并未直接涉及反对观点，但潜在的反对意见可能包括对EDAN工具的准确性、适用性或复杂性的质疑。例如，某些开发者可能认为不同程序或硬件环境下的结果会有所不同，或者认为需要更复杂的分析方法才能得到可靠的结论。

• 评论中未提及具体的技术细节或实例，因此可能存在对EDAN在不同场景下表现的讨论空间。例如，EDAN在处理多线程程序或大规模并行计算时的表现如何，可能会引发进一步的探讨。

• 争议的焦点可能在于EDAN工具是否真的如评论所说那样高效和通用，尤其是在面对复杂或高度专业化的程序时，其分析结果是否足够可靠。

data.title: The international standard for identifying postal items
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了万国邮政联盟（UPU）的S10标准，该标准用于规范国际邮件的追踪号码格式。S10标准采用13个字符，结构包括：前两位为服务标识符，接下来八位为序列号，之后一位为校验码，最后两位为表示始发国的ISO 3166–1国家代码。服务标识符代表不同的邮政服务，如普通信件或包裹邮寄，其中EMS享有“E”前缀。国家可以对某些服务标识符规则进行调整，特别是国内邮寄或与其他国家有协议时。校验码用于纠错，通过特定算法计算。追踪号以条形码形式打印，通常使用Code 128或Code 39格式。这一标准确保了各国邮政服务之间的互通和追踪号码的一致性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于物流系统中序列号和编码标准的讨论，包括其实际容量、算法复杂性以及在不同场景下的应用。

不同观点：
• Ecco 认为中国的物流系统在处理大量包裹时可能会面临序列号不足的问题，尤其是像Shein或Temu这样的平台在短时间内产生的大量包裹，可能导致序列号用尽。
• Forth_fool 指出，8位数的序列号实际上可以产生接近1亿个唯一号码，而不是Ecco所担心的1000万，纠正了对序列号容量的误解。
• Nojs 提到文章中未提及的LPC码，并提供了参考视频，暗示可能有更具体的编码方式未被讨论。
• Bloak 讨论了复杂算法的必要性，质疑用于校验位的复杂算法是否比EAN或13位ISBN使用的简单算法更有优势。
• Lysace 表示对全球标准被广泛接受感到欣慰，认为至少在某些方面可以达成一致。

补充讨论：
• ThePowerOfFuet 提出关于DataMatrix码的问题，尤其是在杂志等邮件上出现的包含收件人全名和地址的码，询问其标准格式和用途，这与前述讨论的序列号问题有一定关联但属于不同应用场景。

争议焦点：主要争议在于序列号是否足够以及复杂算法的必要性。Ecco担心序列号可能不足，而Forth_fool则认为这种担心不必要。Bloak对复杂算法的有效性提出质疑，而Lysace则强调全球标准的一致性带来的好处。

44258633.article_content:
The International Standard for Identifying Postal Items
The Universal Postal Union's S10 standard, in all its glory
Have you ever received a parcel from overseas? I did recently, from Switzerland!
Looking at the envelope, I realised the format of the tracking number (
UT038926726CH
) was in a very similar (if not identical) format to ones I'd used frequently here in the UK.
I'd been receiving emails from Royal Mail about the parcel, so I just presumed that there was some data-sharing agreement in place with Swiss Post and Royal Mail had just given the parcel their own internal reference number.
But seeing the reference number printed on the envelope from the get-go made me want to see what Swiss Post had to say about it...
The same tracking number works across multiple carriers, and it's the same format as all the UK ones! What gives??
Enter: the United Nations Universal Postal Union
The
Universal Postal Union (UPU)
is an agency of the UN that coordinates postal policies to facilitate post flowing across the world. As part of this, it publishes the
S10 standard for the identification of postal items
in a 13-character format - ie. what we've been seeing on our parcels!
If you're interested in learning more about the UPU's interesting 150-year history, you might want to check out
this article
written by fellow webring inhabitant Imaan!
1
Each country's national postal service is assigned as having exclusive reign over S10 codes for that country, and they go about issuing S10 codes from their country.
Tracking Number Format
As it turns out, the structure of our tracking number has a strict design, and our tracking number contains four distinct things:
Character number
Format
Description
1 and 2
2 letters
Service indicator
3 to 10
8 digits
Serial number
11
1 digit
A check digit
12 and 13
2 letters
ISO 3166–1 country code representing the origin of the item
The Service Indicator
The first two characters represent the service that's been used to post the item. There's a fairly extensive list in the standard, with specific options for tracked post, letter post, parcel post... the list goes on. The most interesting part of the service indicators are threefold:
First, there are specific carve-outs in the specification for an organisation called
EMS
- they get all
E
prefixes, so
EA
,
EB
,
EC
, and so on and so forth. EMS is an express international mail service that's run by the UPU itself, but that delegates operations to the national postal services that control their country's S10 codes. This is why you'll not see any way to buy shipping using EMS directly on their website - you buy express international shipping at your local post office and they route it accordingly. It's also worth noting that this only applies to express shipping - not regular-rate traffic.
Second, countries are allowed to override some of the service indicator assignment rules set out in the S10 standard. This can happen when either a parcel is being sent domestically or when a carrier has an agreement with other countries' carriers to reassign some service indicators for other purposes, hence the inclusion of the origin country code to aid interpretation of tracking numbers where this is the case.
Lastly, some service indicators are explicitly disallowed from being used. These are
JA–JZ
,
KA–KZ
,
SA–SZ
,
TA–TZ
and
WA–WZ
since these carry the risk of causing a tracking number to be confused with codes from a different UN data encoding standard.
All in, the possible service indicator space looks like this:
Table source
The Serial Number
This is just a serial number. It's exactly 8 digits long and is generated by the originating carrier as they see fit, provided they don't resue the same number within 12 months. In theory, this means a lost parcel can only be lost for 12 months before it vanishes from the world forever, but in reality, the S10 recommends not reusing a number within a minimum period of 24 months. Even then, you have 10 million parcels per service indicator per country available to be issued, so it's probably not going to be necessary for a carrier to reuse a number for a much longer period of time anyway.
The Check Digit
The check digit corrects any errors in the serial number preceding it, using the following algorithm:
Multiply each digit in the sequence with the corresponding number from this sequence:
8 6 4 2 3 5 9 7
Sum all these values
Divide the sum by 11
Substrac the remainder from 11
If the result is in the range 1-9, use that as the checksum
If the result is 10, use 0 as the checksum
If the result is 11, use 5 as the checksum
This is not a particularly strong checksum, but it's good enough to guard against a couple of accidental digit-swaps here and there. You can play with an interactive demo of it
here
.
Barcode Format
The S10 standard requires tracking numbers to be printed on an item as a barcode, either being in
Code 128
or
Code 39
format.
