data.author: plastic3169
data.article_summary: 这篇文章旨在揭露和澄清有关HDR（高动态范围）和SDR（标准动态范围）之间的一些误解和技术细节。文章首先介绍了基础概念，包括人类对色调的相对感知以及颜色空间的理解。随后，文章比较了SDR和HDR的颜色空间，讨论了两者转换的解决方案。文章还分析了市场上对HDR的一些误导性宣传，如效率问题、色域误解以及创作者意图与自动化处理的冲突。最后，文章提出了应对建议，并总结了要点，强调色调的艺术性而非纯粹的技术性处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HDR与SDR的比较及其在色彩表现上的差异和应用

不同观点：
• **[_wire_]** 认为视频对色彩理论的应用提供了坚实的概述，但指出演示在开篇未能明确提出论点。他强调HDR提供了更高的保真度，可以创造出SDR无法实现的视觉效果，但最终效果仍取决于摄影师的创造力。他还提到，人眼的感知是基于对比度窗口（约100:1），并通过时间调整，而电子显示器的预期使用环境不应影响系统对齐。

• **[dcrazy]** 对演示中的术语简化表示不满，指出演示中将RGB三元组与颜色空间坐标混为一谈，并且未明确解释Rec. 2100颜色空间需要指定传输函数（PQ和HLG）。他还赞赏了演示中的类比（如英尺/米转换）对解释颜色空间转换的帮助。

• **[nayuki]** 对视频的技术传输质量表示赞赏，尤其是视频的快速加载和搜索功能，相比之下对YouTube的用户体验表示不满。

• **[autobodie]** 表示完全同意视频内容，并提到阅读相关书籍后对HDR问题的理解加深，计划广泛分享该视频。

• **[ttoinou]** 认为SDR输入到HDR显示器可以产生与HDR输入相似的效果是显而易见的，但指出HDR作为一种社会运动，不仅仅是数学转换公式，还涉及到工程师、制造商和消费者之间的沟通。他还提到在非现实场景（如 psychedelic 动画）中，更广的色域和更高的位深度能提供更好的视觉体验。

• **[sansseriff]** 赞赏Yedlin以往的工作，但希望他能分享代码以促进开放源代码的色彩分级软件的开发，认为目前最佳的色彩工具多为专有软件，限制了研究的可重复性。

• **[empiricus]** 认为应从接近现实的素材开始，再进行创意处理。SDR类似于黑白电影，而HDR则有机会实现更真实的视觉效果，但目前电影制作者似乎未充分利用这一潜力。

• **[naikrovek]** 将30位色彩的转变与从15位到16位色彩的转变相比较，认为HDR被过度销售为一种全新色彩世界。他还批评电视和显示器制造商将某些功能仅限于HDR模式，而对SDR内容不开放，认为这是不合理的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于HDR与SDR在实际应用中的效果差异，以及HDR作为新技术是否被过度营销。
• 对演示中术语使用和解释的精确性存在不同看法，特别是对颜色空间和传输函数的解释。
• 对开放源代码色彩工具的需求以及专有软件在色彩研究中的限制也被提及。
• 视频技术传输质量的讨论显示了对用户体验的关注，特别是与YouTube的对比。

• **[sansseriff]** 赞赏Yedlin以往的工作，但希望他能分享代码以促进开放源代码的色彩分级软件的开发，认为目前最佳的色彩工具多为专有软件，限制了研究的可重复性。

• **[empiricus]** 认为应从接近现实的素材开始，再进行创意处理。SDR类似于黑白电影，而HDR则有机会实现更真实的视觉效果，但目前电影制作者似乎未充分利用这一潜力。

• **[naikrovek]** 将30位色彩的转变与从15位到16位色彩的转变相比较，认为HDR被过度销售为一种全新色彩世界。他还批评电视和显示器制造商将某些功能仅限于HDR模式，而对SDR内容不开放，认为这是不合理的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于HDR与SDR在实际应用中的效果差异，以及HDR作为新技术是否被过度营销。
• 对演示中术语使用和解释的精确性存在不同看法，特别是对颜色空间和传输函数的解释。
• 对开放源代码色彩工具的需求以及专有软件在色彩研究中的限制也被提及。
• 视频技术传输质量的讨论显示了对用户体验的关注，特别是与YouTube的对比。

data.title: Waymo rides cost more than Uber or Lyft and people are paying anyway
data.author: achristmascarl
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Waymo自动驾驶出租车（robotaxi）服务的价格及其与Uber、Lyft等传统打车服务的比较。根据Obi应用收集的数据，Waymo的平均价格为每趟20.43美元，明显高于Lyft的14.44美元和Uber的15.58美元。尤其是在高峰时段，Waymo的平均价格比Lyft高约11美元，比Uber贵近9.5美元。尽管价格较高，Waymo的受欢迎程度并未减弱，用户对新技术表现出强烈兴趣，70%的受访者表示更喜欢无人驾驶汽车。然而，安全性仍是用户的主要担忧，74%的受访者表示安全是他们最大的顾虑。尽管如此，近40%的用户愿意支付相同或更低的价格乘坐Waymo，而16.3%愿意多支付不超过5美元。文章还指出，Waymo的定价模式不如Uber和Lyft成熟，导致其价格波动较大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Waymo与传统网约车服务（如Uber、Lyft）的比较

不同观点：
• **Waymo体验优于网约车**：多位用户（如harmmonica、tempestn、habosa等）认为Waymo的无人驾驶体验更好，因为每次乘车的质量一致，车辆干净、安全且驾驶平稳。他们还提到不需要与司机交谈、可以自由控制车内环境（如音乐、音量等）是Waymo的显著优势。
  
• **网约车存在不确定性和安全隐患**：一些用户（如rossdavidh、drzaiusx11、mvac）分享了乘坐Uber或Lyft的负面经历，包括车辆状况不佳、司机驾驶技术差或疲劳驾驶等，这些问题在Waymo上不会出现。

• **价格问题**：部分用户（如killion、kellnos）提到Waymo的价格通常较高，但愿意为更好的乘车体验支付溢价。然而，也有用户（如ec109685、kellnos）认为Waymo目前的价格偏高，尤其是在与网约车对比时，并表示不愿意为Waymo支付过高的费用。

• **支持技术发展**：一些用户（如Jelthi）表示他们愿意为支持先进技术付费，尤其是考虑到Waymo提供了高质量、安全的乘车体验，并且无需与司机互动。

• **人类司机的不确定性**：几位用户（如cosmic_cheese、tempestn）提到人类司机可能带来的问题，例如司机取消订单或驾驶不当，而Waymo作为自动驾驶系统不会出现这些问题。

补充讨论：

44258139.article_content:
A central premise of robotaxis is that high usage and lower labor costs will ultimately make it a cheap transportation option. That is still far from true, but now there’s some data that gives us an idea of by how much.
Obi, an app that aggregates real-time pricing and pick-up times across multiple ride-hailing services, has just published what it’s calling the “
first in-depth examination of Waymo’s pricing strategy.
” The company found Waymo’s self-driving car rides to be consistently more expensive than comparative offerings from Uber and Lyft — and it doesn’t seem to matter.
The report, shared exclusively with TechCrunch, is based on a month’s worth of data collected between March 25 and April 25 in San Francisco, California. Obi pulled nearly 90,000 “offer records” from Waymo, Lyft’s “standard” offering, and UberX in order to compare price and ETA. It then compared ride requests from the same times and routes. Obi found Lyft offered the lowest average price at $14.44. Uber was next at $15.58. Waymo’s average price across the month’s worth of data was $20.43.
Image Credits:
Obi
Ashwini Anburajan, Obi’s chief revenue officer, told TechCrunch this was somewhat surprising given the early popularity of Waymo’s service. Waymo said in May it’s providing 250,000
paid trips per week
across its first four cities. Higher pricing has apparently not dimmed that excitement.
“Colloquially, there is an idea that autonomous vehicles are something that will erode driver jobs and put drivers at risk. And I think the irony of what we’ve seen is that it’s actually quite expensive to run an AV, and that that’s not going to be happening, at least in the near term,” she said.
At peak hours, Obi found Waymo’s average price to be about $11 more expensive than a Lyft and nearly $9.50 pricier than an Uber.
“I didn’t expect consumers being willing to pay up to $10 more,” Anburajan said. “I think [that] speaks to a real sense of excitement for technology, novelty, and a real preference to sometimes be in the car without a driver.”

Obi found that not only was Waymo more expensive, but there was greater variability in its pricing than with Uber or Lyft.
Anburajan said one explanation is that Waymo’s pricing model is not as sophisticated. Uber and Lyft, she said, have had more than a decade to refine how they price rides. Those platforms are also a bit more dynamic, with drivers clocking in and out on their own time, or joining or abandoning the gig work altogether.
Waymo, meanwhile, has a mostly fixed but slowly growing supply of vehicles (though the pace of that growth
may soon accelerate
). This has led to what Anburajan said is more of a “pure supply and demand” pricing scheme.
That has two big impacts on customers. One is that short trips tend to cost more than longer ones. Obi found that Waymo rides cost roughly $26 per kilometer if the ride stays under 1.4 km.
This was true of the Uber and Lyft rides, too. But Obi found the shortest Waymo rides were priced 41.48% and 31.12% higher than Uber and Lyft, respectively. That gap shrunk as the rides got longer. In rides lasting between 4.3 km and 9.3 km, a Lyft cost $2.60 per km, an Uber cost $2.90 per km, and a Waymo cost $3.50 per km.
Image Credits:
Obi
The other impact is that longer wait times equals more expensive trips. After all, sending a car a long way to pick up a customer means it will perform fewer high-margin, short-distance rides.
That still isn’t discouraging Waymo customers, Anburajan said, even though Obi found Waymo to have a higher variability in wait times.
In addition to the data-based deep dive, Obi also surveyed riders in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix, Arizona to get a better understanding of what might be driving these trends.
The company found that 70% of users who had taken a Waymo ride said they preferred a driverless car to a traditional rideshare or taxi.
Despite that enthusiasm, Obi found that safety is still a big concern for riders. Of those surveyed, 74% said safety is their biggest concern about robotaxis. Nearly 70% of respondents said they think there should be some form of remote human monitoring of the rides (something that is already a common practice).
Perhaps even more striking is how people answered a question about whether they would be willing to pay more for a Waymo. Nearly 40% said they’d pay “the same or less.” But 16.3% said they’d pay less than $5 more per ride. Another 10.1% said t

data.title: Python argparse has a limitation on argument groups that makes me sad
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何某些浏览器访问博客或wiki时会被阻止。原因在于，为了应对2025年初大量使用旧浏览器用户代理的高流量爬虫（包括用于LLM训练的数据采集），网站采取了封锁措施。如果用户使用最新浏览器却仍被误拦，可联系作者。特别提到，archive.*（如archive.today等）的爬虫因使用旧Chrome用户代理并模仿恶意IP，也被屏蔽，建议使用行为更规范的archive.org进行存档。作者是Chris Siebenmann，2025-02-17发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python程序中处理命令行参数的默认值与用户提供值的优先级问题，以及如何设计参数结构以支持灵活的配置管理。

不同观点：
• [mjevans] 提出是否存在标准Python库来标注一个参数是用户提供的还是默认值，这对于配置优先级管理非常重要。程序的默认值应具有最低优先级，依次被配置文件、命令行参数和运行时更改的配置所覆盖。

• [xg15] 认为设计上可以通过使用如`--foo-timeout=0`来表示禁用某个特定超时，而不是使用`--no-timeouts`来禁用所有超时。这种设计允许用户灵活地控制每个超时，而不是全部一起控制。同时，提出是否可以通过定义别名来实现`--no-timeouts`。

• [NewsaHackO] 建议通过编写一个函数来生成所有参数组，并将每个参数（如`--notimeout`, `--timeout-x`）传递给解析器，以此简化参数的管理。

• [qwertox] 指出问题不在于`add_mutually_exclusive_group`，而在于`argparse`缺少内部机制来优雅地处理这种参数需求。如果不互斥的参数就不应该放在互斥组中。

• [looknee] 提供了一个实际案例，说明gcloud CLI如何使用`argparse`来处理这种情况，通过父互斥组包含一个`--no-timeout`标志和另一个包含具体超时标志的子组。

补充讨论：
• [lordkrandel] 简单表示对该问题的认同，认为确实是个麻烦的问题。

争议焦点：
• 如何设计命令行参数以支持灵活的配置和默认值覆盖逻辑，特别是如何处理多个超时参数的禁用功能。不同的设计方案包括使用`--no-timeouts`完全禁用所有超时与通过特定参数如`--foo-timeout=0`分别控制每个超时。

• `argparse`库的功能限制，尤其是如何在不使用互斥组的情况下处理复杂的参数关系。

44249344.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Apple's Liquid Glass is prep work for AR interfaces, not just a design refresh
data.author: lightningcable
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS设计演变、AR界面设计及其可行性、苹果在AI和设计创新方面的策略

不同观点：
• **支持设计演变观点**：一些用户如[paxys]认为iOS从拟物设计到扁平化设计的转变虽然起初有争议，但最终被整个行业接受，并成为主流设计原则。这种观点认为设计变革往往伴随着争议，但可能最终被广泛接受。

• **反对Liquid Glass和透明UI观点**：[xnx]、[KaiserPro]和[MrThoughtful]等用户批评了Liquid Glass和透明UI设计，认为这些设计在实际使用中存在可读性和可用性问题，尤其是在AR环境中，透明UI会导致能耗问题和视觉混乱。[MrThoughtful]特别提到拟物设计在视觉上更直观和易于理解。

• **质疑AR发展前景观点**：[samwillis]和[Someone1234]对AR技术的发展前景表示怀疑，认为AR眼镜可能只会成为小众产品，且苹果在AR方面的尝试缺乏实质性进展。[Someone1234]指出，关于AR的猜测已经持续多年，但始终没有实质性证据支持这些猜测。

• **支持苹果策略观点**：[bitpush]虽然批评了苹果在AI方面的宣传，但承认苹果可能在设计和整合方面有其独特的策略，而不是单纯追逐当前的AI技术潮流。

• **历史和技术角度观点**：[roughly]从技术角度解释了扁平化设计的优势，如其可扩展性，并预测2027年的iPhone可能揭示苹果在AR和UI设计上的长远规划。[travisgriggs]则从历史角度分析了扁平化设计如何成为一种市场策略，以应对不同设备间的图形表现差异。

补充讨论：
• **设计与科学的混淆**：[jrm4]批评了设计界将时尚与科学混为一谈的现象，认为很多设计决策更多是时尚潮流，而非科学研究结果。

• **设计一致性与设备差异**：[hnlmorg]和[bastawhiz]强调了设计语言一致性的重要性，但也指出不同设备间的交互方式不同，不应该为了设计一致性而牺牲用户体验。[bastawhiz]特别指出，AR/VR界面设计不应强制适用于所有设备形式。

争议焦点：
• **Liquid Glass和透明UI的实际可用性和适用性**：一些用户认为这些设计在AR环境中不切实际，而另一些用户认为这是向AR过渡的必要步骤。

• **AR技术的发展前景和实际需求**：部分用户质疑AR技术的实用性和广泛应用的可能性，而其他用户则认为苹果在AR方面的尝试是具有前瞻性的战略布局。

data.title: I convinced HP's board to buy Palm and watched them kill it
data.author: AndrewDucker
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HP TouchPad和WebOS失败的原因分析，以及对HP公司管理和产品决策的讨论。

不同观点：
• **iconara** 认为HP TouchPad的失败在于产品匆忙上市，缺乏与iPad竞争的生态系统和市场推广，且在评论者因病离开期间，许多错误决策已经做出。
• **ang_cire** 指出Leo Apotheker的管理经验与HP的需求不匹配，董事会未能提出正确的问题，这是导致失败的重要原因。管理技能应与具体业务结合，而非独立存在。
• **joshmarinacci** 作为前Palm员工，认为WebOS的失败归因于Apotheker的战略方向与WebOS不符，且他的到来看似注定了WebOS的终结。若给予更多时间和资金，WebOS本可能成为有力的竞争者。
• **WarOnPrivacy** 对HP品牌整体持负面态度，认为HP长期生产低质量消费产品，其管理层通过糟糕的用户体验和商业策略破坏了品牌价值。
• **phkahler** 质疑评论者将失败归咎于他人的说法，指出在评论者离开期间，产品的发布和取消都是事先计划好的，责任无法完全推脱。
• **paxys** 认为新CEO迅速取消WebOS项目是合理的决策，因为HP无法在移动设备市场中竞争，继续投资只会导致更多资金浪费。
• **Zigurd** 认为WebOS的失败在于其基于Web的技术路线，尽管HP有能力将其发展为竞争平台，但领导层的失败导致其消亡。
• **legitster** 提到在Apotheker之前，HP已经计划放弃消费者市场，内部工程师普遍认为WebOS会被取消。
• **IntrepidPig** 质疑评论者多年后撰文批评他人的动机，认为其推卸责任以推广自己的书籍，且文章风格可疑。
• **b0a04gl** 强调WebOS平台未给予足够时间发展，开发者信任未能建立，失败更多是由于缺乏耐心而非产品问题。
• **lesuorac** 讨论了Apotheker被解雇的时间与WebOS取消的关系，质疑是否有可能通过重命名等方式继续项目。
• **idkwhattocallme** 指出HP错失了将WebOS作为企业OS推广的机会，反而将其作为消费品与iPad竞争，导致策略混乱。
• **timschmidt** 提出一种理论，认为HP TouchPad的设计与iPad过于相似，可能导致苹果与HP之间进行了未公开的法律讨论，最终促成TouchPad的迅速取消。
• **Retr0id** 通过为LG TV开发软件的经历，认为WebOS的核心平台技术优越，但多次易手导致知识流失，特别是在安全和功能开发方面。
• **paultopia** 对HP整体持负面评价，认为其长期缺乏优质产品，仅在低端市场和打印机业务中通过计划报废和订阅模式获利。

补充讨论：
• WebOS的技术潜力被广泛认可，但管理和战略失误导致其未能成功。
• HP董事会和管理层的决策过程被多方质疑，特别是在高管任命和项目取消方面。
• 对HP品牌的整体看法存在分歧，部分评论者对其消费产品质量和商业策略持强烈负面态度。
• 评论中涉及了苹果与HP可能的法律纠纷对TouchPad项目的影响，尽管这是一种未经证实的理论。
• 讨论中多次提到时间和资金的缺乏是WebOS失败的重要因素，显示出对项目支持不足的共识。

data.title: Department of Homeland Security Predator B Drones Are Orbiting over Los Angeles
data.author: vinnyglennon
data.article_summary: 美国海关与边境保护局（CBP）证实，其“捕食者B”无人机（也称为MQ-9“收割者”）正在洛杉矶上空飞行，以应对当地因移民和海关执法局（ICE）行动引发的抗议和暴力事件。尽管这种空中监视引发了侵犯隐私和违宪的争议，CBP表示这些无人机仅用于支持联邦执法部门，不会监视第一修正案活动。社交媒体上已有证据显示这些无人机在洛杉矶执行任务，采用六边形轨道模式进行监视。尽管具体无人机型号尚不明确，但此类行动在其他城市也曾发生过。

U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has been flying its Predator B drones, also commonly referred to
by their military variant designation of MQ-9
Reapers, over Los Angeles as part of the U.S. government’s response to the
unrest there
, the agency confirmed to us on Wednesday. The flights are in response to protests that
escalated to violence
on multiple occasions, following a massive operation by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last Friday.
Persistent aerial surveillance like this has long been controversial, with civil rights advocates saying it violates the right to privacy and undermines
the Constitution
. At the same time, the fact that a drone is doing it largely evokes a uniquely upsetting response. While using the Predator Bs over urban locales is rare, it’s not unprecedented, and manned platforms do this kind of work every day across the country.
CBP’s Air and Marine Operations (AMO) “MQ-9 Predators are supporting our federal law enforcement partners in the Greater Los Angeles area, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement, with aerial support of their operations,” spokesman John Mennell told us Wednesday afternoon in response to our query earlier this week. “Additionally, they are providing officer safety surveillance when requested by officers. AMO is not engaged in the surveillance of First Amendment activities.”
U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed that its Predator B drones have been flying over Los Angeles in connection to the unrest there.(CBP)
CBP
CBP had been mum about the issue for days, even though open-source reporting on social media had already presented compelling evidence of the drones’ orbits. On June 9, user @Aeroscout on X posted air traffic control (ATC) audio stating that two “Q-9s” – call signs TROY 703 and TROY 701, had passed each other in airspace over Yuma, Arizona, as one was replacing the other over Los Angeles. @Aeroscout had previously posted ATC audio of TROY 701 checking in on Los Angeles Center Sector 09. A short time later, Alaska Flight 1020 was given a traffic advisory for “drone traffic.”
I've confirmed that the two targets operating in hexagonal surveillance orbits over DTLA these past 36 hours are both MQ-9s, callsigns TROY701 and 703
As 703 replaced 701, they passed each other in the airspace near Yuma, AZ where I found this needle in the haystack! Listen 📻
pic.twitter.com/MWPjFIOvgc
— Aeroscout (@aeroscouting)
June 9, 2025
"TROY701"
Department of Homeland Security MQ-9 over Los Angeles this evening. It's been operational for over 9 hours now.
📻 Heard working 128.600 Los Angeles Center, Sector 09 at 16:45z, 8 June 2025
pic.twitter.com/YAtaAYlmbE
— Aeroscout (@aeroscouting)
June 9, 2025
While there has not yet been any explicit identification of the “Q-9s” as CBP Predator Bs, TROY is a known Department of Homeland Security (DHS) callsign. TROY 314, a CBP Multi-Role Enforcement Aircraft (MEA) based on the Beechcraft King Air 350ER twin-engine turboprop, and a CBP Black Hawk helicopter using the callsign TROY 212, were also tracked over Los Angeles this weekend.
Homeland Security ISR bird running ovals over
#Paramount
earlier; now over Los Angeles proper.
🇺🇸 TROY314 is Beechcraft Scorpion N251J
#A25BFD
pic.twitter.com/yI3EdlEpZN
— Evergreen Intel (@vcdgf555)
June 7, 2025
One high flier conducting intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance over the riots/protests in downtown LA at 2326z in support of the Dept. of Homeland Security.  TROY212 is a DHS/CBP H-60 Blackhawk that some have reported flying low in the area.  The remaining appear to be…
pic.twitter.com/Kc8slkUg0h
— TheIntelFrog (@TheIntelFrog)
June 8, 2025
Furthermore, plane trackers using online software first began noticing aircraft flying hexagonal patterns over Los Angeles on Sunday. Though not always the case, this is indicative of CBP Predator B surveillance patterns observed in the past. This includes the use of one of the
CBP Q-9s over Minneapolis back in 2020.
Hexagons aren't always MQ-9s, but in this case, yes, there are two MQ-9 Reapers over LA today. Just ridiculous.
pic.twitter.com/tMsUAbIeL4
— John Wiseman (@lemonodor)
June 9, 2025
NOW:
@CBP
Predator Drone
#CPB104
circling over Minneapolis at 20K feet. Took off from Grand Forks Air Force Base.
#Minneapolisprotests
#surveillance
#planespotting
pic.twitter.com/hVYF4GXe1Y
— Jason Paladino (@jason_paladino)
May 29, 2020
CBP has MQ-9s at three locations: the National Air Security Operations Centers in Sierra Vista, Arizona (located on Fort Huachuca), San Angelo in Texas, and Grand Forks in North Dakota.
What specific version or versions of the CBP Predator B have been flying over Los Angeles is unclear. The TROY 701 callsign was tied to a particular tail number, CBP-113,
back in April
, but it is not clear if that same

data.title: High-volume exercise tied to increased coronary artery calcification score
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一项发表于《JACC: Advances》的研究显示，高运动量训练的男性运动员相比非运动员，其冠状动脉钙化（CAC）评分更高，尤其是运动量超过3,000 MET-分钟/周的男性运动员。然而，运动量在1,500至3,000 MET-分钟/周的男性运动员或运动量超过1,500 MET-分钟/周的女性运动员中未发现CAC评分差异。研究强调了性别的显著影响，并指出需要更多高质量的纵向研究来深入理解运动对动脉粥样硬化的影响，以及确定最佳运动量标准。一项作者披露了与制药和医疗技术行业的联系。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：运动量与冠状动脉钙化（CAC）之间的关系，特别是高运动量对不同性别运动员的影响。

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：评论者认为研究结果显示每周运动量超过3,000 MET-分钟的男性运动员，其冠状动脉钙化分数高于非运动员男性，这表明极高运动量可能对心脏健康有负面影响。评论者进一步解释，3,000 MET-分钟相当于每天运动7小时，每周七天，认为这对绝大多数人来说并不构成问题，因为很少有人能达到这个运动量。

• 第二种观点：评论者指出，对于每周运动量在1,500到3,000 MET-分钟之间的男性运动员，以及运动量超过1,500 MET-分钟的女性运动员，研究未发现其CAC分数有显著差异。这表明适度的高运动量可能不会对心脏健康产生明显负面影响。

补充讨论：
• MET-分钟的概念：评论者表示对MET-分钟的具体含义不了解，但通过计算得出3,000 MET-分钟相当于每天运动7小时。这表明对MET-分钟这一单位缺乏了解可能影响对研究结果的正确解读。

• 争议焦点：高运动量是否会对心脏健康产生负面影响。研究结果显示，只有极高运动量（>3,000 MET-分钟/周）的男性运动员表现出较高的CAC分数，而其他运动量范围内的运动员则未见此趋势。这引发了关于运动量与心脏健康关系的进一步讨论和研究的需求。

44277820.article_content:
May 28, 2025
The GIST
High-volume exercise tied to increased coronary artery calcification score
by Lori Solomon
edited by
Andrew Zinin
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
reputable news agency
proofread
Male athletes with high-volume exercise training have a higher burden of calcified plaque than male nonathletes, according to a review published in the June issue of
JACC: Advances
.
Ahmed Abdelaziz, M.D., from the Medical Research Group of Egypt at the Negida Academy in Arlington, Massachusetts, and colleagues evaluated the impact of endurance exercise on coronary atherosclerosis assessed by cardiac computed tomography in athletes and nonathletes. The analysis included data from nine
observational studies
(61,150 participants).
The researchers found that male athletes with an exercise volume of >3,000 MET-minutes/week showed higher mean coronary artery calcification (CAC) scores than nonathlete males (mean difference = 31.62). No difference in CAC was found for male athletes with 1,500 to 3,000 MET-minutes/week or
female athletes
with an exercise volume of 1,500 MET-minutes/week or greater. There were significant sex-specific differences for the association between exercise volume and calcified plaque number and volume by coronary computed tomography angiography.
"Future high-quality
longitudinal studies
are imperative to address these gaps, refine our understanding of the impact of exercise on atherosclerosis, clarify the prognostic value of subclinical
coronary atherosclerosis
in athletes and establish standardized thresholds for optimal exercise volume," the authors write.
One author has disclosed ties to the pharmaceutical and medical technology industries.
More information:
Ahmed Abdelaziz et al, Sex Differences in the Impact of Exercise Volume on Subclinical Coronary Atherosclerosis,
JACC: Advances
(2025).

data.title: GitHub's CEO says startups can only get so far with vibe coding
data.author: kmdupree
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用“vibe coding”（依赖AI辅助编程）在开发中的作用和效果的讨论，以及AI在创业公司和技术投资中的影响。

不同观点：
• **fnordpiglet**：认为vibe coding在项目的初始阶段非常有用，可以帮助处理许多基础性、琐碎的设计决策。但当项目复杂度增加时，AI往往会陷入局部最小值，难以继续推进，最终需要更有经验的工程师接手。他将这种体验比作与有4年经验的工程师合作，能够解决一定问题，但面对复杂问题时仍需更有经验的人来领导。

• **nico**：提出创业公司在初期通过AI辅助编程来快速构建系统并推向市场，可以更早获得投资者的青睐。即使后期需要更多人力投入，早期通过AI节省成本和时间可能会吸引更多投资，形成一种“超精益公司”模式。

• **duxup**：对“vibe coding”这一概念表示困惑，认为它似乎是为了吸引媒体关注而创造的词汇，而非一个明确的技术概念。

• **sherdil2022**：支持nico的观点，认为nico的评论具有一定的合理性。

• **jamesgill**：质疑AI在实际商业环境中的应用，提到微软（GitHub的拥有者）在AI上投入巨大资金（800亿美元），暗示AI技术尚未成熟到能完全替代人类开发者，公司仍然需要大量投资来推进AI相关技术。

补充讨论：
• **fnordpiglet**的评论中提到了AI在处理工具库和细节方面的能力，但也指出了AI在面对复杂问题时的局限性，强调了人类工程师经验的重要性。
• **nico**则侧重于AI在商业和创业环境中的潜力，认为AI可以帮助创业公司快速成长，即使在后期需要更多人力投入，早期的优势仍然明显。
• **duxup**和**sherdil2022**的评论则反映了部分人对“vibe coding”这一新兴概念的理解和态度，有人表示困惑，有人表示支持。
• **jamesgill**的评论引入了大公司（如微软）在AI领域的巨额投资，质疑AI在当前技术水平下能否真正替代人类开发者，并指出AI技术本身仍需大量资源支持。

争议焦点：AI在编程中的实际效用和局限性，以及在创业公司和技术投资中的潜在影响。

data.title: A receipt printer cured my procrastination
data.author: laurieherault
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者如何通过理解电子游戏的成瘾机制来克服拖延症。作者多年来尝试了各种提高生产力的方法，但都效果不佳。通过观察自己在玩游戏时能够长时间专注，他开始研究游戏如何通过快速重复的“游戏循环”和即时强烈的“反馈”来吸引玩家。作者将这种机制应用到日常任务中，把任务分解成更小的微任务，并通过完成任务后立即给予反馈（如揉掉便签纸）来增强动力和成就感。最终，他使用热敏打印机打印待办清单，并结合游戏化的任务分解和反馈机制，成功改善了拖延问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过任务管理系统应对拖延症，以及使用热敏打印机生成纸质任务单的优缺点。

不同观点：
• Laurieherault（作者）分享了自己应对拖延症的方法，并期待得到反馈。这种方法是通过将任务分解为微任务来实现的，作者对此感到兴奋并希望对其他有同样问题的人有所帮助。
• Whalee对使用热敏纸打印任务单的健康风险提出警告，指出接触热敏纸（尤其是常接触的情况下）可能存在健康隐患，如BPA/BPS暴露。
• StandardUser提出了高生产力状态下的心理负担，认为维持高标准的任务管理可能会导致心理压力，并产生“不可避免的系统崩溃”的恐惧感。此外，维持高生产力往往会引发更多的任务，形成恶性循环。
• Jw1224支持使用热敏打印机进行任务管理，并分享了自己通过Raspberry Pi自动打印任务的系统，同时提醒使用无酚热敏纸以避免毒性问题。
• Xp84将该任务管理方法与迪士尼的员工调度系统（CDS）进行了类比，认为这种纸质任务单系统在实际操作中非常高效，能够优化人员调度和任务分配。
• Abalone认为可以通过数字化任务管理系统（如Apple Notes）获得类似的满足感，并且数字系统具有节省纸张、易于调整优先级等优点。
• Tekkk对任务管理系统的长期有效性提出质疑，认为任何系统在没有外部压力、适当的营养和锻炼的情况下都会失效，强调身体健康对生产力的影响。
• Fidotron讨论了物理任务单和数字任务表示之间的差异，认为物理任务单可能更能激发行动力，并质疑UI设计是否可以通过更加拟物化来减少对物理打印机的需求。
• Noelia-分享了自己使用便利贴管理任务的失败经验，并表示有兴趣尝试热敏打印机来简化任务管理流程。
• Tines提出了对任务管理系统引入游戏化元素的担忧，认为这可能加剧人们对即时反馈和外部肯定的依赖，引用Neil Postman的“娱乐至死”理论，强调无聊和自我调节的重要性。
• Dackle提到了David MacIver的每日任务列表系统，认为从空白列表开始可以更好地过滤出真正重要的任务，并分享了自己通过笔记本应用实现类似任务管理的经验。
• Vidarh支持将任务分解为微任务的策略，并分享了自己通过键盘快捷键将任务移到完成列表以获得满足感的做法。
• Reverendsteveii将任务管理系统与健身计划结合，分享了自己通过白板任务管理实现健身目标的经验，认为多重反馈循环可以保持长期动力。
• Dclowd9901分享了通过早晨整理床铺来获得心理平静和满足感的做法，认为这种小习惯可以带来积极的心理影响。

补充讨论：
- 使用热敏纸打印任务单的健康风险，尤其是BPA/BPS暴露问题，是一个值得关注的讨论点。
- 高生产力状态下的心理负担和任务管理系统的长期有效性是另一个讨论焦点。
- 物理任务单与数字任务管理系统的优缺点对比，以及游戏化任务管理可能带来的负面影响，也是讨论中的重要内容。
- 最后，小习惯如整理床铺对心理状态的积极影响也被提及。

44256499.article_content:
A receipt printer cured my procrastination
How I can focus on my to-do list by understanding the science of video games
Why can I focus for hours on a game but procrastinate when writing an email? For over 20 years, I've tried everything to boost my productivity. I've read dozens of books and tested many methods. Nothing made a real difference. But I finally found a solution by understanding what makes video games addictive. And a thermal receipt printer will become the best investment of my life.
My fight against procrastination
I started my business when I was 21 (I'm now 39). I built custom apps and did consulting for accounting software, invoicing systems, and point-of-sale tools.
Procrastination has always been my biggest struggle. The only way I could get things done was by relying on stress, coming from clients or financial pressure. That worked for a while, but it cost me my health (I burned out) and my business (I went bankrupt).
I noticed that I have no problem spending hours fully focused on a video game. If I can focus on a game, then my brain must also be capable of focusing on other tasks. So I naturally started asking myself why it's so easy to get hooked by a game, and how I could apply that same effect to tasks I struggle to complete.
It turns out that many of the struggles I've had throughout my life are linked to ADHD (Attention Deficit Disorder). The goal of this article isn't to focus on ADHD, but it's important to mention. ADHD affects many people, often without them even knowing it, in various ways and at different levels.
Why video games hook us
To understand what makes a video game addictive, let's take first-person shooters (FPS) as an example. FPS games are among the most popular and addictive games.
An FPS is built around a simple loop:
Aim
→
Shoot
→
Hit
or
Miss
. This is the
game loop
. The outcome, hit or miss, is immediately shown through sounds or visuals. This immediate reaction is called
feedback
.
For a game to be addictive, the game loop must repeat frequently and give strong feedback. Imagine an FPS where you only meet an enemy every 30 minutes. That wouldn't be engaging. The loop must repeat quickly to keep you interested.
Feedback in FPS games has improved a lot over time. Early FPS games only showed a simple blood splash when you hit an enemy. Modern games provide much stronger feedback. Now, when you hit an enemy, you might see:
the crosshair briefly changes to confirm the hit
damage numbers pop up above the enemy
sound effects
enemy death animations
a progress bar filling up
a new skill unlocked
random reward
and more...
Note that a game can have several game loops. For example, there can be another loop for finding random equipment for your character. Feedback can also come from outside the main loop, such as loot boxes or side missions.
For a game loop to be addictive, other factors matter too. You need to personally enjoy the type of game, and the challenge must match your skill level. If it's too easy or too hard, you won't be hooked. There are dozens of other factors, unique to each player's personality and preferences.
When all these elements come together, each game loop gives you a small dose of dopamine and creates a state of
flow
. In this state, we're fully focused, we lose track of time, and it's easier to handle complex tasks.
One final point: Video games are
easy to start
. They require very little motivation or discipline to start playing.
Key Takeaways:
The game loop should repeat often.
Feedback from the loop should be strong.
Games are easy to start, even with low motivation.
How to apply the feedback loop to our tasks
Based on what we've just seen, our real-life
game loop
is made up of completing tasks and habits throughout the day.
Our first goal is to
repeat this game loop as many times as possible each day
. A simple solution is breaking tasks into smaller parts. Let's take an example everyone can relate to: cleaning the house. At first glance, you might break down "Clean the house" like this:
Clean the house
Clean the kitchen
Clean the office
Clean the bedroom
...
If these three tasks take about an hour, that's only three game loops. Another problem is starting a task. Cleaning your bedroom might take 20 minutes, which feels too long when you're not motivated. So you procrastinate.
My solution is breaking things down even further:
Clean the house
Kitchen
Wash dishes
Wipe down surfaces
Clean floor
Take out trash

44256499.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者如何通过理解电子游戏的成瘾机制来克服拖延症。作者多年来尝试了各种提高生产力的方法，但都效果不佳。通过观察自己在玩游戏时能够长时间专注，他开始研究游戏如何通过快速重复的“游戏循环”和即时强烈的“反馈”来吸引玩家。作者将这种机制应用到日常任务中，把任务分解成更小的微任务，并通过完成任务后立即给予反馈（如揉掉便签纸）来增强动力和成就感。最终，他使用热敏打印机打印待办清单，并结合游戏化的任务分解和反馈机制，成功改善了拖延问题。

data.title: Luxe Game Engine
data.author: garrypettet
data.article_summary: Luxe是一款跨平台的快速开发游戏引擎，支持Mac、Linux、Windows和Web，正在开发主机支持。该引擎易于学习，专注于2D游戏开发，同时具备强大的3D渲染能力。Luxe强调设计和工作流，方便快速表达创意，特别适合个人开发者及团队使用。它使用C++编写，但游戏通常用定制版的Wren语言开发，未来支持更多语言。Luxe具有模块化设计，提供灵活的工具集，支持自定义工作流和编辑器，以适应不同游戏需求。其渲染器易于学习且高度灵活，适合快速迭代和实验。目前，Luxe已推出预览版，并提供社区和开发日志支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Luxe引擎的优缺点及适用场景

不同观点：
• [shayway] 认为Luxe和Wren都过于结构化且不够灵活。相比高层次的引擎如Godot，Luxe显得不够易用；而相比低层次的控制，如Raylib，Luxe又显得不够灵活。Shayway认为Luxe更适合工作室工作流，尤其是注重艺术家工具链，而Godot更适合小型独立项目。此外，Luxe的文档和示例较少，学习曲线较高。

• [joeld42] 则对Luxe引擎持积极态度。他称赞Luxe的脚本编写符合人体工程学，性能较好，且可以通过Wren编写原生扩展模块。此外，Wren的纤维功能在处理游戏逻辑时表现优秀，图形模块高度可配置，工具链设计精良。Joeld42认为Luxe适合从小型游戏到大型项目的多种规模开发，并且更新频繁且有清晰的迁移策略，非常适合小型团队和实验性工作流。

• [josephcsible] 指出Luxe的“限制”部分与自由开源软件（FOSS）不兼容，并且对于不关心FOSS的开发者来说，Luxe相比Unity和Unreal没有明显优势。

• [999900000999] 认为Luxe虽然不错，但不如真正的开源解决方案，尤其是Godot，目前仍是最好的FOSS引擎，仅次于Unity和Unreal。

• [krapp] 质疑Luxe引擎的实际应用情况，询问是否有人使用该引擎成功发布过游戏。

补充讨论：

Luxe引擎是否真正适合小型独立开发者以及其在开源和商业应用中的定位问题。一方认为Luxe对小型项目和独立开发者友好，另一方则质疑其在FOSS领域的竞争力和实际应用案例。

44269270.article_content:
Try luxe now!
About
luxe is a cross platform, rapid development game engine
to make games for
Mac, Linux, Windows, and Web
, with console support in development.
luxe is an easy to learn game engine for making 2D or 3D games.
As an engine it prioritizes design and workflow for rapidly expressing ideas.
Designed as a 2D first engine
, luxe aims to provide a strong 2D toolset
ready
to make games. This applies whether it's a one hour or one+ year project.
Beyond the 2D layer lives a powerful but accessible hardware driven renderer, with great support for shaders, asset pipelines, render paths and more.
This allows 3D rendered games to use luxe all the same.
luxe itself is written in c++
, although luxe games will usually be made in a custom version of the
Wren
programming language. Later, any language that can interact with C can be used.
Read on further for more details about luxe!
Made by a game studio
luxe is
used to make games
by the engine developers directly.
We've always believed an engine is driven by real world use, so we made a game studio around it because that's what makes sense to us. We're making
Mossfield Origins
and
Mossfield Archives
.
We're a
diverse game studio with a strong vision
for good community, sustainable business, empowered workers and empowering more voices to create games.
Development status
luxe is
now available
in preview!
try the luxe preview here!
Development updates
Sign up for the luxe mailing list
Don't miss when luxe becomes available!
We'll only email for important development news or access.
sign up for the mailing list
Join the community
Visit the
'create with luxe' community
.
You can also
join the
discord
.
Read the latest dev logs
Most recent - a series on using luxe:
dev log #11 -
modifiers
dev log #12 -
custom modifiers
dev log #13 -
scenes
dev log #14 -
projects
dev log #15 -
try luxe now!
Design philosophy
Modular
A tightly designed core engine with a module system ensures a lightweight yet expressive set of tools.
Fluid
The heart of luxe is rapid iteration and expression of intent. These are design pillars, because workflow matters.
For humans
Built by people that make games with it, luxe cares about the people that are using it day to day.
Workflow
The
luxe editor
is optional?
luxe is for solo developers as well as teams, so while it provides
a great code based workflow
, it is not limited to code only.
editors and tools
enhance the luxe workflow, which empowers artists, designers and programmers in the expression of ideas, and rapid game development.
The editor is
designed for game specifics
, just like the rest of the engine, so custom/project editors are easy, and shareable via modules.
editors help to build worlds, animation, ui and more
Tools, not features
worlds, modifiers, entities and systems
Games are a diverse medium with unique challenges. luxe makes the distinction between tools and features explicit, and
builds around tools as a core principle
.
This frees the engine from being bloated by things a fraction of games want, and instead
aims to empower games to be specific, adaptive and exact
. At runtime, you only pay for what you use.
By combining systems both high and low level,
luxe is like a toolbox, and a game is the connection of these into a whole.
When configuring a
type
of project to reuse (like a 2D platformer or 3D first person project), luxe provides
outlines
, which jump start projects into predefined workflows.
Outlines are where custom workflows are defined
above the engine level.
luxe provides pieces that snap together,
ready
to make games
Rendering for everyone
luxe is powered by an easy to learn but highly flexible renderer
Games can have unique needs, and game specific choices.
luxe allows games to choose the best suited rendering style for their world
, and offers high level interaction from the game.
With a full abstraction over portable backends, a new shading language designed with the luxe philosophy, and a scripted pipeline driven workflow,
rendering is right at home in luxe.
Rendering is a complex field where
fast iteration is important, and experiments can be done quickly and easily
. luxe aims for that, and to be approachable, so that beginners can learn foundations without starting from scratch.
Modular by design
luxe is built around a modular package system
luxe has a rich set of systems
ready
to make games,
but it couldn't possibly provide
all
systems that
all
different types of games need
, without becoming bloated or unfocused.
When the engine doesn't provide something, it's often by design.
Modules
serve this need by providing a way for you to expand the tools and systems that are available to you when making games. Modules also provide ways to use other programming languages.
This modularity is a fundamental part of luxe,
even the luxe API itself is a module.
Read the luxe blog
Sign up for the luxe mailing list
Don't miss the latest updates!

data.title: Subtype Inference by Example
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了通过类型推断和子类型推断来改进编程语言的类型系统，以提升代码质量和程序员效率。传统的Hindley-Milner类型推断系统缺乏子类型支持，导致类型约束传播不灵活，产生不必要的类型错误。Stephen Dolan在其博士论文中提出了支持完整子类型的**代数子类型**（Algebraic Subtyping）系统，但该论文过于学术化，缺乏实际实现指导。

作者基于代数子类型，提出了更易理解和高效的**立方双向统一**（cubic biunification）方法，避免了复杂的数学证明，提供了逐步代码示例。子类型推断的优势在于它能根据数据流方向推断兼容类型，而非强制类型相等，从而减少类型错误。这种方法还允许语言设计者实验更复杂的静态分析，而无需程序员手动添加类型注解。

然而，立方双向统一的最坏时间复杂度为O(n³)，相比Hindley-Milner的线性复杂度O(n)，在性能上可能成为瓶颈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：类型系统及其简化，特别是子类型推断和类型注解的实用性

不同观点：
• **tomp** 认为Lionel Parreaux的SimpleSub工作相比Stephen Dolan的MLsub算法更简单有效。tomp指出，Dolan的主要贡献在于类型语言的设计，而非算法本身。Parreaux通过去除正负类型的假设进一步简化了类型系统，这显示出进一步的改进潜力。

• **juancn** 讨论了静态类型系统的实际应用，强调了类型注解的重要性。尽管承认类型注解可能影响代码美观，juancn认为它们有助于代码阅读和理解，尤其是对代码功能的明确表达。

• **abeppu** 对历史上类型系统的研究与现代工作进行了比较，特别提到了Hindley-Milner系统和System F<:。abeppu质疑Dolan在2016年的工作与20世纪80-90年代的研究有何不同，并寻求明确的新贡献或突破。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现的复杂性**：tomp强调了Parreaux通过SimpleSub对Dolan的MLsub进行的简化，显示出算法实现上仍有改进空间。

• **类型注解的实用性争议**：juancn支持类型注解在代码可读性和维护性方面的实用价值，尽管这与其他开发者可能偏好自动类型推断的立场存在潜在分歧。

• **历史与现代研究的对比**：abeppu提出了对类型系统研究进展的疑问，希望厘清现代研究在几十年前工作的基础上有何创新和进展。

争议焦点：
• **简化与实用性的平衡**：在类型系统的简化和实际应用中的复杂性之间如何取得平衡，是讨论中的一个潜在争议点。

• **类型注解的价值**：类型注解在代码可读性和开发效率上的价值存在不同看法，部分开发者可能更倾向于依赖类型推断。

• **现代研究的新贡献**：对类型系统的研究在几十年间的进展和创新点需要进一步澄清，以明确现代研究的新颖之处。

44231044.article_content:
In recent years, there has been increasing interest in tools and programming languages that can automatically detect common types of bugs, in order to improve product quality and programmer productivity. Most commonly, this is done via
static type systems
, but traditional static type systems require large amounts of manual annotation by programmers, making them difficult to work with. Therefore, modern programming languages make increasing use of
type inference
, which provides the same benefits with few or no manual type annotations required.
The most popular form of type inference is based on the
Hindley-Milner
system, which is limited by its lack of support for
subtyping
. In
his 2016 PhD thesis
, Stephen Dolan introduced
Algebraic Subtyping
, a new type inference system with full subtyping support. However, as an academic thesis,
Algebraic Subtyping
is an intimidating 157 pages full of formal mathematical proofs and short on practical implementation guidance.
As someone who has spent much of the subsequent three and a half years understanding algebraic subtyping and trying to implement it in practical programming languages, I want to share the results of my studies. In this series of blog posts, I will show you how to actually implement algebraic subtyping, or rather, an improved version I call
cubic biunification
which is faster and easier to understand, with detailed, step-by-step code examples and zero mathematical proofs.
What is subtype inference and why is it important?
Most current languages with type inference use some variation of the Hindley-Milner system, which is based around
unification
, the process of iteratively
equating
types to solve constraints. Unfortunately, this results in a system which is inflexible and unintuitive, leading to many language specific hacks and extensions in an attempt to work around the resulting issues.
With unification, values that are used together are forced to have the same type. If you pass a value to a function, it’s not enough for that value to have a type
compatible
with the function’s argument type. Unification forces it to be
equal
to the function’s argument type. If you pass two different values to the same function, they are forced to have the same type. Effectively, type constraints are propagated both forwards
and backwards
relative to the dataflow of your program, which is confusing and leads to many type errors that do not reflect real bugs in the underlying program logic. A number of workarounds have been developed to avoid this issue in specific cases, but the underlying problem persists in any HM-derived inference system.
With subtyping by contrast, type inference is based around ensuring that each value has a type
compatible
with its usages. Constraints follow the data flow of your program but do not flow “backwards”, so there are no spurious type errors just because you happened to pass two different values with different, but compatible, types in the same place. This makes type inference much more powerful and also more intuitive.
Furthermore, I think that evaluating subtype inference in the context of existing programming languages and paradigms undersells its potential, because it facilitates new styles of programming that are largely unexplored. In particular, most programming languages are reliant on programmer supplied type annotations, which means that each feature in the type system must have corresponding syntax in type annotations and must be easy to write concisely in said syntax. In effect, the type system is limited by the need to maintain a convenient manual type syntax.
The ability to typecheck an entire program with no manual type annotations removes this constraint and means that the programming language designers are free to experiment with new and more sophisticated types of static analysis with no burden on the end user. (Hindley-Milner of course does not require manual type annotations either, but the lack of subtyping makes its use less practical).
For example, the programming language Rust has structurally inferred traits (
Send
,
Sync
, etc.) used to statically ensure properties such as thread safety and unwind safety. By default, a new type in Rust is considered thread safe if all of its components are thread safe and so on, meaning that the safety checks operate largely automatically with only the occasional need for explicit concern from the programmer. The subtype inference system presented here is capable of implementing similar features with minimal changes to the compiler, making it easy to experiment with adding such safety checks with no changes required to the end user code base.
That sounds great! What’s the catch?
There are a couple of obstacles I see towards fulfilling the vision outlined above:
Performance
Hindley-Milner style type inference runs in approximately linear O(n) time for monomorphic code. Cubic biunification by contrast has worst case cubic O(n³) time complexity, hence the name. Subtype base
44231044.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了通过类型推断和子类型推断来改进编程语言的类型系统，以提升代码质量和程序员效率。传统的Hindley-Milner类型推断系统缺乏子类型支持，导致类型约束传播不灵活，产生不必要的类型错误。Stephen Dolan在其博士论文中提出了支持完整子类型的**代数子类型**（Algebraic Subtyping）系统，但该论文过于学术化，缺乏实际实现指导。

作者基于代数子类型，提出了更易理解和高效的**立方双向统一**（cubic biunification）方法，避免了复杂的数学证明，提供了逐步代码示例。子类型推断的优势在于它能根据数据流方向推断兼容类型，而非强制类型相等，从而减少类型错误。这种方法还允许语言设计者实验更复杂的静态分析，而无需程序员手动添加类型注解。

然而，立方双向统一的最坏时间复杂度为O(n³)，相比Hindley-Milner的线性复杂度O(n)，在性能上可能成为瓶颈。

data.article_summary: **QRKey** 是一个命令行工具，用于生成和恢复用于离线私钥备份的QR码。它可以将文件转换为QR码并打印或存储，随后通过扫描这些QR码恢复文件。该工具支持大文件，可将文件拆分为多个QR码，并包含元数据以便于恢复和验证。用户可以通过Homebrew或Docker安装和使用该工具。主要功能包括从文件生成包含QR码的PDF，以及从PDF或文本文件中扫描QR码恢复文件。项目采用MIT许可证，已获得136个星标。

QRKey
qrkey
is a command-line tool for generating and recovering QR codes from files for offline private key backup.
It allows you to convert files into QR codes that can be printed or stored, and later recovered from those QR codes.
It supports large files by splitting them into multiple QR codes, and includes metadata for easy recovery and validation.
Convert a file into a PDF with QR codes
Recover from a PDF with QR codes with a barcode scanner
Recover from a PDF with QR codes from a file with lines
Installation
macOS users can install
qrkey
using Homebrew Tap:
brew tap techwolf12/tap
brew install techwolf12/tap/qrkey
For Docker users, you can use the Docker image:
docker run -v
"
$(
pwd
)
"
:/mnt ghcr.io/techwolf12/qrkey:latest generate --in /mnt/testfile.txt --out /mnt/test.pdf
For other systems, see the
releases page
.
Usage
To generate a QR code from a file, use the following command:
qrkey generate --in
<
file
>
--out file.pdf
To recover a file from QR codes, use the following command:
qrkey recover --in
<
file.txt
>
Or to recover interactively:
qrkey recover

data.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting: Our Search for a Time-Series Foundation Model
data.author: tiwarinitish86
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了时间序列预测领域中“基础模型”（foundation models）的兴起，这些模型旨在通过大规模预训练来适应多种数据流和领域，而无需为每个场景单独训练模型。作者对比了传统模型如ARIMA和Prophet，指出其在面对多样化数据时的局限性，并介绍了亚马逊、谷歌、IBM和Datadog的最新时间序列基础模型（Amazon Chronos、Google TimesFM、IBM Tiny Time-Mixers、Datadog Toto）。

文章详细描述了这些新模型的评估方法，包括使用多变量预测任务和真实数据源。通过实验，作者评估了这些模型在零样本预测（zero-shot forecasting）中的表现，发现基础模型在处理不同类型的时间序列数据时展现了较强的泛化能力，能够有效减少手动调参和重新训练的工作量。

最终，作者认为时间序列基础模型具有巨大的潜力，特别是在可观察性数据处理方面，能够显著提升预测效率和适应性。未来，进一步优化和应用这些模型将是关键。

Introduction
In the last few years, the field of time-series forecasting has seen a fundamental shift. Where we once depended solely on classic statistical methods, think
ARIMA
,
SARIMA
, and
Prophet
, new “foundation” models have emerged, promising to bring the power and flexibility of large language models (LLMs) into the world of time-series data. The allure is obvious: can we build a single, reusable forecasting model that works across a variety of datasets and domains, instead of painstakingly training a new model for every scenario?
Parseable
is built to handle our users’ observability data at any scale, a nonstop stream of raw ingest counts, infrastructure vitals, and fine-grained application signals. Running a separate, hand-tuned forecasting model for every slice quickly turns into a treadmill: each new stream or workload tweak demands fresh hyper-params, retrains, and ever-growing config sprawl. All that manual churn slows forecasts and breeds drift, so the results never feel fully trustworthy.
Then came the rise of foundation models, which revolutionised natural language processing by offering strong zero-shot and transfer learning capabilities. Researchers began asking a natural question: if LLMs can generalise to new tasks with minimal retraining, could similar techniques be applied to time-series data? What if you could just hand any telemetry stream to a pre-trained foundation model and immediately get a high-quality forecast, regardless of whether the model had seen data from that source before?
Motivated by this possibility, we set out to benchmark a new generation of time-series foundation models,
Amazon Chronos
,
Google TimesFM
,
IBM Tiny Time-Mixers
, and
Datadog Toto
.
Our goal was to assess how well these models perform on two representative tasks: a relatively straightforward forecasting problem (predicting ingestion volumes) and a more complex multivariate problem (forecasting multiple pod-level metrics). Along the way, we compared them to classical baselines and took note of both practical and technical trade-offs.
This post details our methodology, the challenges we encountered, how we evaluated the models, and what we learned from putting foundation models to the test on real-world observability data.
Why Foundation Models?
The idea of “foundation models” has fundamentally changed how we approach complex machine learning problems. In natural language processing, models like GPT have shown that a single, large model trained on vast and diverse datasets can generalize well to entirely new tasks sometimes even without fine-tuning. This zero-shot capability means a single model can perform sentiment analysis, summarization, translation, or question-answering, just by changing the prompt.
In the world of time-series forecasting, the appeal of such flexibility is obvious, especially for modern data engineering and observability platforms. Traditionally, every new data stream whether it’s CPU utilization, request rates, or disk I/O required its own model, hyperparameter tuning, and regular retraining. For an SRE or platform engineer, this quickly becomes unmanageable as the number of streams explodes. If a pipeline ingests data from a hundred microservices, does every service metric really need its own hand-tuned ARIMA or Prophet model? The answer, up until recently, was “yes.”
Foundation models for time series are built to change that. The core motivation is scalability and adaptability: train a single, large model (often with billions of parameters) on a wide range of time-series datasets and let it learn the underlying “language” of temporal data. Once trained, this model should ideally handle a completely new telemetry stream, even if it has never seen data of that exact shape or domain before. In theory, you could input any new time series, whether it’s network packet counts, database query durations, or energy consumption readings and get a high-quality forecast without retraining.
This is a huge leap from traditional approaches. Classic statistical models like ARIMA or seasonal decomposition excel when you have clean, stationary data and a wel
44265833.article_summary:
文章探讨了时间序列预测领域中“基础模型”（foundation models）的兴起，这些模型旨在通过大规模预训练来适应多种数据流和领域，而无需为每个场景单独训练模型。作者对比了传统模型如ARIMA和Prophet，指出其在面对多样化数据时的局限性，并介绍了亚马逊、谷歌、IBM和Datadog的最新时间序列基础模型（Amazon Chronos、Google TimesFM、IBM Tiny Time-Mixers、Datadog Toto）。

文章详细描述了这些新模型的评估方法，包括使用多变量预测任务和真实数据源。通过实验，作者评估了这些模型在零样本预测（zero-shot forecasting）中的表现，发现基础模型在处理不同类型的时间序列数据时展现了较强的泛化能力，能够有效减少手动调参和重新训练的工作量。

最终，作者认为时间序列基础模型具有巨大的潜力，特别是在可观察性数据处理方面，能够显著提升预测效率和适应性。未来，进一步优化和应用这些模型将是关键。

主要讨论点：时间序列基础模型（foundation model）的有效性、应用及其评估方法

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby认为，博客中对时间序列基础模型的定义有误。基础模型应该具备处理训练目标任务之外的多任务能力，而博客中讨论的是无需重新训练的分布外预测。Fripplebubby指出，现有的ARIMA和Prophet模型已经很好地解决了这个问题，且重新拟合模型只需很短的时间。此外，他认为LLM架构是否能提升单变量或多变量时间序列预测任务仍未有明确答案。

• wenc提到了Makridakis竞赛的历史结论，即复杂的统计方法未必比简单方法提供更准确的预测。wenc质疑当前是否情况有变，并引用了Nixtla与Chronos团队在相关问题上的争论。

• nikhil4usinha关注模型的实际应用场景，尤其是异常检测方面的用例。

• fumeux_fume对结果表中模型是否在相同数据集上测试表示困惑，并建议提供测试数据和预测的可视化图表以增加透明度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是时间序列基础模型的定义及其评估标准是否恰当。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是不同评估方法和数据集的选择对模型表现的影响。
• 测试方法的科学性和评估指标的合理性也是讨论中的重要议题。

这些观点共同构成了对时间序列基础模型及其应用的多元看法，涉及模型评估、测试方法、应用场景等多个方面。

data.title: A dark adtech empire fed by fake CAPTCHAs
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 2024年，安全研究人员发现克里姆林宫支持的虚假信息活动利用恶意广告技术绕过社交媒体审核，传播亲俄罗斯的虚假新闻。这些活动通过一个名为“Doppelganger”的网络进行，该网络使用复杂的“域名伪装”技术，使虚假信息网站在线时间更长，并确保只有特定受众能看到内容。Doppelganger与VexTrio共享基础设施，后者是一个恶意流量分发系统，管理来自钓鱼网站和社交工程诈骗的流量。研究显示，Doppelganger的伪装服务还推广成人约会网站，如LosPollos和TacoLoco，这些网站通过入侵WordPress网站获取流量，并利用诱导性通知进行诈骗。Adspro Group运营这些服务，其基础设施由瑞士 hosting providers C41和Teknology SA提供支持，最终追溯到由Giulio Vitorrio Leonardo Cerutti拥有的公司。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TacoLoco网络使用欺骗性手段通过浏览器推送通知进行流量变现，以及相关技术和社会工程学诈骗的问题。

不同观点：
• LegionMammal978：分享了亲身经历，一位老年亲属曾被TacoLoco的推送通知骚扰，表明这种欺骗性手段对不熟悉技术的用户影响很大。他通过设置浏览器自动拒绝通知来解决问题。
• preinheimer：认为通过“点击按钮证明你是人类”的诈骗手段很巧妙，能有效欺骗用户。
• justusthane：对为何在访问虚假新闻内容前要经过多个域名跳转表示不解，并询问这种行为的目的。
• b0a04gl：将这种推送通知视为新的弹出广告，认为浏览器赋予其过多的前台展示权限，且未征求用户同意。
• psychoslave：指出TacoLoco的流量分配系统（TDS）主要管理来自钓鱼、恶意软件和社会工程诈骗的受害者流量，并批评合法广告网络的类似操作。
• thyristan：批评浏览器在权限请求和管理方面的用户界面设计混乱，建议统一权限请求和更改流程，增加更多的控制选项。
• tempodox：感叹诈骗手段的创造力不断提升，使得网络欺诈更加猖獗。
• BMaronge：认为文章对链接跳转多次的解释不够清晰，质疑诈骗者为何不直接跳转。
• HocusLocus：分享了帮助家人防范诈骗的经验，强调对老年人的网络安全教育重要性，并提到国家行为者参与的网络诈骗问题。
• username223：质疑为何JavaScript能够发送操作系统级别的通知，认为应限制不可信代码的运行权限，避免将“开放网络”变成攻击面。
• tehwebguy：庆幸某些移动平台不允许浏览器推送通知，认为这是有效的防范措施。
• StuntPope：对文章中提到的“克里姆林宫虚假信息”持怀疑态度，认为Krebs的文章带有偏见，并质疑其专业性。
• wwn_se：推荐使用Adblock作为解决方案，建议为家人和朋友启用广告拦截以防止被骗。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是浏览器在处理推送通知和其他权限请求时的用户界面设计是否合理，thyristan对此提出详细批评并建议改进。
• 另一个讨论点是为何诈骗者要通过多个域名跳转来引导用户访问虚假内容，justusthane和BMaronge对此表示不解。
• 对Krebs文章中提到的“克里姆林宫虚假信息”存在不同看法，HocusLocus和StuntPope对此有不同解读和评价。
• 对于如何防范此类诈骗，用户提出了不同建议，包括设置浏览器自动拒绝通知、使用Adblock、以及加强网络安全教育等。

Late last year, security researchers made a startling discovery: Kremlin-backed disinformation campaigns were bypassing moderation on social media platforms by leveraging the same malicious advertising technology that powers a sprawling ecosystem of online hucksters and website hackers. A new report on the fallout from that investigation finds this dark ad tech industry is far more resilient and incestuous than previously known.
Image: Infoblox.
In November 2024, researchers at the security firm
Qurium
published an investigation into “
Doppelganger
,” a disinformation network that promotes pro-Russian narratives and infiltrates Europe’s media landscape by pushing fake news through a network of cloned websites.
Doppelganger campaigns use specialized links that bounce the visitor’s browser through a long series of domains before the fake news content is served. Qurium
found
Doppelganger relies on a sophisticated “domain cloaking” service, a technology that allows websites to present different content to search engines compared to what regular visitors see. The use of cloaking services helps the disinformation sites remain online longer than they otherwise would, while ensuring that only the targeted audience gets to view the intended content.
Qurium discovered that Doppelganger’s cloaking service also promoted online dating sites, and shared much of the same infrastructure with
VexTrio
, which is thought to be the oldest malicious traffic distribution system (TDS) in existence. While TDSs are commonly used by legitimate advertising networks to manage traffic from disparate sources and to track who or what is behind each click, VexTrio’s TDS largely manages web traffic from victims of phishing, malware, and social engineering scams.
BREAKING BAD
Digging deeper, Qurium noticed Doppelganger’s cloaking service used an Internet provider in Switzerland as the first entry point in a chain of domain redirections. They also noticed the same infrastructure hosted a pair of co-branded affiliate marketing services that were driving traffic to sketchy adult dating sites:
LosPollos[.]com
and
TacoLoco[.]co
.
The LosPollos ad network incorporates many elements and references from the hit series “Breaking Bad,” mirroring the fictional “Los Pollos Hermanos” restaurant chain that served as a money laundering operation for a violent methamphetamine cartel.
The LosPollos advertising network invokes characters and themes from the hit show Breaking Bad. The logo for LosPollos (upper left) is the image of Gustavo Fring, the fictional chicken restaurant chain owner in the show.
Affiliates who sign up with LosPollos are given JavaScript-heavy “
smartlinks
” that drive traffic into the VexTrio TDS, which in turn distributes the traffic among a variety of advertising partners, including dating services, sweepstakes offers, bait-and-switch mobile apps, financial scams and malware download sites.
LosPollos affiliates typically stitch these smart links into
WordPress
websites that have been hacked via known vulnerabilities, and those affiliates will earn a small commission each time an Internet user referred by any of their hacked sites falls for one of these lures.
The Los Pollos advertising network promoting itself on LinkedIn.
According to Qurium, TacoLoco is a traffic monetization network that uses deceptive tactics to trick Internet users into enabling “push notifications,” a
cross-platform browser standard
that allows websites to show pop-up messages which appear outside of the browser. For example, on Microsoft Windows systems these notifications typically show up in the bottom right corner of the screen — just above the system clock.
In the case of VexTrio and TacoLoco, the notification approval requests themselves are deceptive — disguised as “CAPTCHA” challenges designed to distinguish automated bot traffic from real visitors. For years, VexTrio and its partners have successfully tricked countless users into enabling these site notifications, which are then used to continuously pepper the victim’s device with a variety of phony virus alerts and misleading pop-up messages.
Examples of VexTrio landing pages that lead users to accept push notifications on their device.
According to
a December 2024 annual report
from
GoDaddy
,
nearly 40 percent of compromised websites in 2024 redirected visitors to VexTrio via LosPollos smartlinks
.
ADSPRO AND TEKNOLOGY
On November 14, 2024, Qurium
published research
to support its findings that LosPollos and TacoLoco were services operated by
Adspro Group
, a company registered in the Czech Republic and Russia, and that Adspro runs its infrastructure at the Swiss hosting providers
C41
and
Teknology SA
.
Qurium noted the LosPollos and TacoLoco sites state that their content is copyrighted by
ByteCore AG
and
SkyForge Digital AG
, both Swiss firms that are run by the owner of Teknology SA,
Giulio Vitorrio Leonardo Cerutti

data.title: Have a damaged painting? Restore it in just hours with an AI-generated "mask"
data.author: WithinReason
data.article_summary: 麻省理工学院的研究生Alex Kachkine开发了一种使用数字构造膜物理修复原始画作的新方法。该方法通过打印极薄的聚合物膜，形成一个可以对齐并粘贴到画作上的“面具”，以覆盖和修复受损区域，且该膜可以轻松移除。这种技术可以在几个小时内完成传统修复方法需要数周甚至更长时间的工作。例如，Kachkine在3.5小时内修复了一幅15世纪的油画，而传统方法可能需要更久。同时，数字记录可以保存修复细节，供未来修复者参考。不过，Kachkine也强调，任何修复都应与了解画作历史和来源的保护专家协商，以确保修复的伦理性和适当性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：艺术品修复中的伦理问题、技术应用及其长远影响

不同观点：
• [bee_rider] 认为艺术品修复涉及伦理问题，即修复是否符合艺术家原始意图和风格。他提出一个有趣的观点，即当代艺术家可以事先说明他们接受的修复计划，但同时也指出，艺术品随着时间损坏本身也讲述了一个历史故事，因此即使得到艺术家许可，修复也可能存在争议。

• [contravariant] 对修复方法本身更感兴趣，并认为尽管方法本身比AI更具创新性，但为了获得资金支持，将其描述为AI技术是必要的。

• [omoikane] 引用了数字记录在未来修复中的潜在价值，但也指出数字记录需要定期更新以确保其可读性，并通过一个漫画链接（xkcd）来加强这一点。

• [amelius] 以幽默的方式表达了对AI修复可能出现错误的担忧，特别是提到AI生成图像时可能出现的明显错误（如七根手指的手）。

• [absurdo] 对讨论中没有提到某个相关人物（ Baumgartner）表示奇怪，暗示在该话题中这一参考的缺失是不寻常的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于艺术品修复是否应严格遵循艺术家原始意图，以及即使有艺术家许可，历史痕迹的保留是否也应被考虑。
• 数字技术在修复中的应用及其长期可靠性也被提及，特别是数字记录的保存和更新问题。
• 对AI技术在修复中可能出现的技术性错误的幽默批评，反映了人们对新技术应用的潜在担忧。

Art restoration takes steady hands and a discerning eye. For centuries, conservators have restored paintings by identifying areas needing repair, then mixing an exact shade to fill in one area at a time. Often, a painting can have thousands of tiny regions requiring individual attention. Restoring a single painting can take anywhere from a few weeks to over a decade.
In recent years, digital restoration tools have opened a route to creating virtual representations of original, restored works. These tools apply techniques of computer vision, image recognition, and color matching, to generate a “digitally restored” version of a painting relatively quickly.
Still, there has been no way to translate digital restorations directly onto an original work, until now. In a
paper
appearing today in the journal
Nature
, Alex Kachkine, a mechanical engineering graduate student at MIT, presents a new method he’s developed to physically apply a digital restoration directly onto an original painting.
The restoration is printed on a very thin polymer film, in the form of a mask that can be aligned and adhered to an original painting. It can also be easily removed. Kachkine says that a digital file of the mask can be stored and referred to by future conservators, to see exactly what changes were made to restore the original painting.
“Because there’s a digital record of what mask was used, in 100 years, the next time someone is working with this, they’ll have an extremely clear understanding of what was done to the painting,” Kachkine says. “And that’s never really been possible in conservation before.”
As a demonstration, he applied the method to a highly damaged 15th century oil painting. The method automatically identified 5,612 separate regions in need of repair, and filled in these regions using 57,314 different colors. The entire process, from start to finish, took 3.5 hours, which he estimates is about 66 times faster than traditional restoration methods.
Kachkine acknowledges that, as with any restoration project, there are ethical issues to consider, in terms of whether a restored version is an appropriate representation of an artist’s original style and intent. data.title: Infinite Grid of Resistors
data.author: niklasbuschmann
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一个经典的电阻网格谜题，该网格由无限延伸的方形晶格组成，每对相邻节点之间有一个电阻R。文章主要探讨如何计算相邻节点之间的有效电阻。通过考虑电流场的对称性和叠加原理，文章得出相邻节点间的有效电阻为R/2。这种方法类似于电偶极子的电势场分析，利用了拉普拉斯方程的对称性。然而，文章也指出，该推导依赖于一些假设，例如电流在“无限远处”的行为，而这些假设并未完全严谨证明。特别是，将电流注入无限网格的设想存在问题，因为理论上节点到无限远的电阻是无限大的。尽管如此，通过简单对称性得出的结果R/2与其他方法验证结果一致。文章最后提到，要使论证更严谨，可以考虑有限大小的网格。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• 不同背景的人（如数学家与电气工程师）对问题的理解和态度不同，电气工程师更关注实际应用和测量问题，而数学家可能更关注抽象的理论问题。
• 有人认为这类问题是教授们用来“折磨”学生的工具，而另一些人则认为在实际应用中（如有限网格）还是有其价值的。

Remain, remain thou here,

There is a well-known puzzle based on the premise of an
infinite grid of resistors connecting adjacent nodes of a square lattice. A
small portion of such a grid is illustrated below.
Between every pair of adjacent nodes is a resistance R,
and were told that this grid of resistors extends to infinity in all
direction, and were asked to determine the effective resistance between two
adjacent nodes, or, more generally, between any two specified nodes of the
lattice.
For adjacent nodes, the usual solution of this puzzle is
to consider the current flow field as the sum of two components, one being
the flow field of a grid with current injected into a single node, and the
other being the flow field of a grid with current extracted from a single
(adjacent) node. The symmetry of the two individual cases then enables us to
infer the flow rates through the immediately adjacent resistors, and hence we
can conclude (as explained in more detail below) that the effective
resistance between two adjacent nodes is R/2. This solution has a certain
intuitive plausibility, since its similar to how the potential field of an
electric dipole can be expressed as the sum of the fields of a positive and a
negative charge, each of which is spherically symmetrical about its
respective charge. Just as the electric potential satisfies the Laplace equation, the voltages of the grid nodes satisfy the discrete from of the Laplace equation, which is to say, the voltage at each node is the average of the voltages
of the four surrounding nodes. Its also easy to see that solutions are
additive, in the sense that the sum of any two solutions for given boundary
conditions is a solution for the sum of the boundary conditions.
If we accept the premise of an infinite grid of resistors,
along with some tacit assumption about the behavior of the voltages and
currents at infinity, and if we accept the idea that we can treat the
current fields for the positive and negative nodes separately, and that
applying a voltage to a single node of the infinite grid will result in some
current flow into the grid, the puzzle is easily solved by simple symmetry
considerations. We assert (somewhat naively) that if we inject (say) four
Amperes of current into a given node, with no removal of current at any
finite point of the grid, the current will flow equally out through the four
resistors, so one Ampere will flow toward each of the four adjacent nodes.

that adjacent node, as indicated in the left hand figure below.
The figure on the right shows the four nodes surrounding
the negative node, assuming we are extracting four Amperes from that node
(with no current injected at any finite node of the grid). Again, simple
symmetry dictates the distribution of currents indicated in the figure.
Adding the two current fields together, we see that the link between the
positive and negative nodes carries a total of 2 Amperes away from the
positive node, and the other three links emanating from the positive node
carry away a combined total of 1 + 1 + 1

the same current as all the other paths, so the resistance of the direct link
equals the effective resistance of the entire grid excluding that link. The
direct link is in parallel with the remainder of the grid, so the combined
resistance is simply R/2.

right answer (as can be verified by other methods), but the premises are
somewhat questionable, and the reasoning involves some subtle issues that

data.title: Chicken Eyeglasses
data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: 鸡眼镜是一种小型眼镜，设计用于防止鸡之间的啄羽和同类相食行为。与遮眼片不同，鸡眼镜允许鸡向前看，同时遮挡特定视野以减少攻击性行为。早期20世纪在美国大规模生产和销售，通常由赛璐珞或铝制成，通过鼻孔固定。一些款式使用玫瑰色镜片，据信能掩盖血液颜色，从而减少啄伤，但效果存在争议。鸡眼镜曾是断喙术的替代方法，但因涉及组织穿刺，在某些国家被禁止。虽然已不再生产，但仍被作为收藏品，并在流行文化中出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于给鸡佩戴眼镜或接触镜片的讨论，涉及其用途、历史实践和实际效果。

不同观点：
• **MaDeuce** 提到一个哈佛商学院的案例研究 "Optical Distortion, Inc"，介绍了一种为鸡设计的接触镜片。该用户强调了市场进入策略的必要性，包括价格、销售团队的规模和地点，并提供了经济效益的数据支持。

• **thomassmith65** 提到通过一个播客了解到鸡眼镜的概念，并提供了相关播客的链接，显示出通过不同媒体接触到这一信息的途径。

• **ortusdux** 分享了20世纪70年代在一家研究实验室工作的经验，当时通过用热铁烫卷鸡的喙来防止啄伤，并认为给鸡戴眼镜的解决方案更好。这提供了一个历史背景，比较了过去与现代的动物福利实践。

• **WastedCucumber** 对鸡眼镜如何防止啄伤表示怀疑，指出只有在1911年的一篇文章中提到这种眼镜是为了保护鸡的眼睛，而不是明确为了防止啄伤。这质疑了鸡眼镜的实际功效。

• **CompoundEyes** 仅仅表示这个话题让他感到开心，没有深入讨论，但显示出对话题的兴趣和积极情绪。

• **smusamashah** 提到无法找到维基百科文章中描述的鸡佩戴那些特定眼镜的图片，对信息的真实性和可视证据提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了鸡眼镜或接触镜片的实际用途，尤其是在防止鸡之间啄伤方面的效果。
• 提到了历史上的动物处理方法，如烫卷鸡喙，与现代方法进行对比。
• 对鸡眼镜的实际效果和可视证据存在一定的怀疑和争议。
• 讨论通过不同的信息源展开，包括学术案例、播客和维基百科，显示出信息获取的多样性。

争议焦点：鸡眼镜是否真的能有效防止啄伤，以及其实际应用和历史实践的对比。

44244675.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Small eyeglasses made for chickens
1911 newspaper story on chicken eyeglasses from the
Spirit Lake Beacon
(Iowa)
[
1
]
Chicken eyeglasses
, also known as
chicken specs
,
chicken goggles
, generically as
pick guards
, and under other names,
[
2
]
were small
eyeglasses
made for
chickens
intended to prevent
feather pecking
and
cannibalism
. They differ from
blinders
in that they allow the bird to see forward, whereas blinders do not. One variety used
rose-colored
lenses, as the coloring was thought to prevent a chicken wearing them from recognizing blood on other chickens, which may increase the tendency for
abnormal injurious behavior
. They were
mass-produced
and sold throughout the United States as early as the beginning of the 20th century.
[
3
]
[
4
]
Description and purpose
[
edit
]
Chicken eyeglasses were often made from celluloid or aluminum
[
5
]
and typically consisted of "two oval panels that fit over the upper beak of the chicken. A pin is put through the nostril to hold the oval pieces in place."
[
2
]
Different designs were produced that attached to the chicken's head in different ways. Some were held in place by a strap,
[
3
]
some by small hooks into the
nares
(nostrils) and some by piercing the bone
septum
between the nostrils with a
cotter pin
.
[
6
]
Due to the piercing of tissue, this last type of design is illegal in some countries.
[fn. 1]
Some versions of the devices had semi- or fully transparent lenses, whereas others were tinted, often red- or rose-colored. Other designs were
blinders
, which are opaque and prevent entirely forward vision.
[
2
]
[
7
]
The intended purposes of chicken eyeglasses were to prevent aggressive pecking, cannibalism, and feather pecking.
Chicken eyeglasses are an alternative to
beak trimming
, which removes approximately one-third of the beak by a cold or heated blade or an infrared beam, usually when chicks are one day old. Beak trimming is often effective in reducing pecking injuries but causes pain and significantly affects chicken welfare.
[
7
]
[
8
]
[
9
]
[
10
]
[
11
]
Red-tinted lenses
[
edit
]
Red-tinted lenses were considered effective in reducing internecine pecking because they disguise the color of blood.
[
7
]
As summed up in a 1953 article in Indiana's
National Road Traveler
newspaper, "The deep rose-colored plastic lenses make it impossible for the cannibal [chicken] to see blood on the other chickens, although permitting it to see the grain on the ground."
[
12
]
Elmer Haas of the National Band & Tag Company, a major producer of rose-colored chicken eyeglasses, whose grandfather had devised wireframes for chickens in 1902,
[
13
]
indicated that he believed the purported blood-masking effect of the rose coloring was a myth: "the firm added the rose-colored glasses because it indulged the chicken owners ... [c]hickens are color blind".
[
13
]
(In fact, chickens, like other birds, have good
color vision
.
[
14
]
)  The firm had added the rose-colored feature to its glasses in 1939 under the brand name "Anti-Pix."
[
15
]
This variety of eyeglasses was more complicated than others because the red lenses were fixed to a hinge at the top of the frame. As the hen lowered its head to feed, the lens swung out, giving it an unobstructed view of the ground. When the hen raised her head, as she would during aggression, the lens would swing down giving the hen a red-tinted perception of the environment.
[
16
]
Rose-colored
contact lenses
, rather than eyeglasses, have also been proposed to reduce cannibalism in chickens.
[
17
]
History
[
edit
]
Detail from a 1903 patent filed by Andrew Jackson Jr.
A form of chicken eyeglasses was first patented in 1903 by Andrew Jackson Jr. of
Munich
,
Tennessee
, as an "Eye-protector for chickens."
[
18
]
In the U.S., they were available through the mail order company
Sears-Roebuck
or chicken feed stores for a few cents.
[
19
]
The eyeglasses are no longer produced by the National Band & Tag Company, but are sought as
collector's items
.
[
6
]
Using chicken eyeglasses was still practiced in 1973, evidenced by Illinois'
The Hawk-Eye
newspaper that a farmer had 8,000 chickens fitted with the rose-colored variety.
[
20
]
One inventor of a form of the glasses proposed legislation in
Kansas
to require
all
chickens in the state to be fitted with glasses, but his campaign was unsuccessful.
[
21
]
In popular culture
[
edit
]
On January 16, 1955, Sam Nadler of the National Farm Equipment Company of Brooklyn appeared on
CBS
' popular primetime television show,
What's My Line?
[
22
]
The show was in the format of a
guessing game
, in which a panel attempted to determine the line (occupation) of contestants.
[
23
]
Show officials listed Mr. Nadler's occupation for the audience as "sells 'eyeglasses' for chickens". After the panel was unsuccessful in guessing his occupation,  Mr. Nadler's identity was revealed, and he stated that his company sold 2–3 million pairs of chicken eyeglasses annually.

• **MaDeuce** 提到一个哈佛商学院的案例研究 "Optical Distortion, Inc"，介绍了一种为鸡设计的接触镜片。该用户强调了市场进入策略的必要性，包括价格、销售团队的规模和地点，并提供了经济效益的数据支持。

• **thomassmith65** 提到通过一个播客了解到鸡眼镜的概念，并提供了相关播客的链接，显示出通过不同媒体接触到这一信息的途径。

• **ortusdux** 分享了20世纪70年代在一家研究实验室工作的经验，当时通过用热铁烫卷鸡的喙来防止啄伤，并认为给鸡戴眼镜的解决方案更好。这提供了一个历史背景，比较了过去与现代的动物福利实践。

• **WastedCucumber** 对鸡眼镜如何防止啄伤表示怀疑，指出只有在1911年的一篇文章中提到这种眼镜是为了保护鸡的眼睛，而不是明确为了防止啄伤。这质疑了鸡眼镜的实际功效。

• 讨论中涉及了鸡眼镜或接触镜片的实际用途，尤其是在防止鸡之间啄伤方面的效果。

data.title: Wrong ways to use the databases, when the pendulum swung too far
data.author: luuio
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者作为初级开发人员时在一家公司经历的数据库使用不当的问题。最初，公司的关键系统依赖于包含大量存储过程的SQL Server数据库，这些存储过程包含复杂的业务逻辑，导致API调用占用大量数据库服务器CPU资源，并且由于查询计划的变化经常引发超时和死锁，最终导致系统可靠性下降。为了解决这些问题，公司决定进行系统重写，但新的设计完全摒弃了关系型数据库，转而采用简单的键值存储（Key-Value stores）。然而，这种设计并不适合高度关系型的数据模型，导致了一系列新的问题。文章强调了从错误中学习的重要性，并反思了设计选择对系统的影响。

44260964.article_content:
Wrong ways to use the databases, when the pendulum swung too far
Date: June 11, 2025
Tags:
software development
Disclaimer: This story took place when I was a junior developer for a previous employer ages ago. Some details might be fuzzy, and goes without saying this is entirely from my own POV so take everything here with humor and a grain of salt.
I like to share these stories, because I believe learning what
not
to do is just as valuable as learning what to do.
The setup
The team I joined was part of a larger org. This org inherited a highly critical pipeline from an offshore team. When I say critical, I mean the-entire-company-bottom-line-and-financials-depended-on-them critical. I guess the company just wanted to move that particularly branch of development back to the US. These systems were complex with a lot of business rules and many moving parts, multiple large code bases, and definitely ancient.
The development experience wasn’t great either. Even though there were separate codebases, the projects were somehow setup in a way that changing one small file required building almost the entire thing (which took about 15-30 minutes). The build process also depended on the underlying operating system components, thus development had to happen inside a VM. Each VM had a “dev” version of the entire pipeline deployed, that’s the only way one could exercise the code while under development. Then one would have to know which DDL files they needed to copy from the build output to the local “dev” deployment and restart all the right Windows services in order to test their changes.
Tests were flaky, outages all the time, random hidden undocumented features everywhere. Things were… quirkly, to say the least. One particular quirk that’s the main character of this story is the databases–the main source of the outages, as I could remember.
The pendulum swung left: the old database
All the data for this pipeline was spread across multiple SQL Server databases, across different servers. That wasn’t the problem. The problem was that a lot of business logic was baked into pages and pages of stored procedures, with joint after joint after joint that would put Snoop to shame. Why was it written that way? Nobody knew. Perhaps some small part of the original team got tired of the bad development process, and it was quicker to just update stored procedures than having to wait for half an hour for compilation.
Thinking back, the data wasn’t modeled badly either. Even more than a decade later, I still think that the domain is pretty complex, and the data was modeled as well as anyone could have.
This little quirk meant a few things:
Many critical APIs call would spend most of its CPU time inside the finite database servers. New APIs, or updating existing APIs meant you were hogging the DB/CPU time from every one else.
API latency was at the mercy of the Query Planner. Any slight change in data statistics or business logic would cause the a different Query Plan to be picked, which drastically changed the execution time, and usually caused timeouts. A hash join suddenly became a full table scan across billions of rows without any warning.
The cherry on top of all that was the entire pipeline, from stored procedure to managed and native code, heavily used
MSDTC
–which was brital and proned to deadlocks.
All of this tanked the pipeline reliability. Downtime was largely due to deadlocks, or some query timing out, which had been running just fine minutes earlier.
To this org’s credit, they put a lot of time and effort into improving things, and made a lot of progress, but a rewrite was inevitable.
Interlude:
I will refrain from discussing whether a rewrite was truly necessary. I didn’t know all the details then, and I don’t know all the details now. But we can discuss the design choices of the rewrite.
The pendulum swung right: the new design
Perhaps due to the scars from the existing database issues, “the architects” decided they wanted nothing to do with relational databases, nor stored procedure, nor query plans. They wanted everything to be written into simple primitive Key-Value stores for their new design.
Each instance of these key value stores provided exactly 4 and only 4 operations: Read one key, Insert one key/value pair, Update key/value pair, Delete one key. No transactions, no batching, nothing else.
For some products, that’s perfectly fine, but not for this pipeline. And here comes a chain of “fun” events, one influenced by a previous decision:
The data schema
The data for this domain is highly relational, but perhaps modeling things the right way, it could still work with a KV store. Instead of modeling things in a relational manner, one could write nested documents, and embed the child elements inside the parent document. So to get the items related to a parent object, one just loads the entire document for the parent object, no need for fancy joints.

data.author: insistent

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLM）在医疗诊断中的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby认为，临床医生经过训练能够有效地从患者那里提取必要的信息，即使患者遗漏或隐瞒信息。然而，研究表明，即使在虚构场景中，参与者也未能有效地传达必要的信息，这表明LLM在实际应用中可能无法像医生一样有效地提取信息。
• zora_goron从自身经验出发，指出医学教育在临床实践中的重要性，认为真正的临床教育在医学院之后才开始，呼应了医学教育与实际操作之间的差距。
• twotwotwo讨论了在工作环境中使用LLM时遇到的问题，特别是模型在需要澄清信息时表现不佳。他提出了一些改进方法，如通过训练和提示来提高模型的信息提取能力。
• dosinga认为，LLM在识别病因和推荐医疗行动方面表现出色，但在人类自我诊断时表现不佳，这可能是因为人类与LLM互动过程中出现的问题。
• wongarsu建议进行更深入的研究，设置两个对照组：有LLM辅助的人类、有医生辅助的人类和无辅助的人类，以更好地理解LLM在诊断中的实际效果。
• dhash对研究表示赞赏，并提出未来研究可以关注专家用户（如医生）与LLM的比较，以及LLM在实际医疗环境中的表现和影响。
• ekianjo对LLM与人类在诊断中的表现持积极态度，认为即使LLM表现与对照组无异，也显示出其替代人类的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 研究方法和数据公开：bryant提到研究数据和方法已在GitHub上公开，供进一步分析。
• 改进方向：twotwotwo和dhash都提到可以通过训练、提示工程和模型改进等方式来提高LLM在实际应用中的表现。
• 争议焦点：LLM在实际医疗诊断中是否能够达到或接近医生的水平，特别是在信息提取和与患者互动方面。

data.title: Fixing the mechanics of my bullet chess
data.author: tibbar
data.article_summary: 作者Jacob Brazeal分享了他下国际象棋时的一个发现。他一直擅长快棋（blitz），但在超快棋（bullet）中表现较差。最近，他改变了移动棋子的方式，从拖放（drag-and-drop）改为点击（click-and-click），结果每步平均节省0.25秒，使他的超快棋等级分（ELO）提高了约100分。点击移动不仅更快，尤其是在长距离移动棋子时，还能更好地预判走子，避免失误。这一改变让作者在超快棋中思考时间更充裕，减少了仓促走子导致的错误，缩小了与快棋的等级分差距。他感叹这一简单的技术调整竟然带来显著提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同用户对国际象棋快棋（bullet）中使用触摸屏还是鼠标更有效的讨论，以及对具体操作方式（点击移动与拖拽移动）的偏好。

不同观点：
• helloplanets认为触摸屏（尤其是平板）在快棋中非常有效，因为可以多指点击移动，操作直观快捷。同时，还指出了对“Elo评分”的术语使用建议（应为小写的“Elo”）。
• fasterik则认为这取决于玩家的鼠标技能，并指出大多数顶级快棋玩家（如Andrew Tang、Hikaru Nakamura、Daniel Naroditsky）使用拖拽移动，只有Magnus Carlsen例外，但他认为Magnus的快棋实力主要来源于其基础棋艺，而非移动速度。
• jpablo强烈反对点击移动比拖拽移动快的观点，认为点击移动多了两次额外的动作（按下和松开），而拖拽移动可以在等待对手走棋时进行预判和取消，有助于避免最后一刻的失误。他质疑是否有顶级快棋或超快棋玩家使用点击移动，并提到Magnus Carlsen曾在旧视频中使用点击移动，但不确定他在其他平台是否如此。
• pvg简短地表示，高动作频率（APM）在国际象棋中同样重要。
• snitty以幽默的语气表示，只使用支持vim键位绑定的国际象棋工具，暗示对操作方式有个人偏好。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于点击移动与拖拽移动的效率问题，jpablo和fasterik对此有直接的分歧。
• 讨论中提到了顶级玩家的操作习惯，尤其是Magnus Carlsen的操作方式成为争论的一个例子。
• 术语使用的准确性也被提及，helloplanets指出了“Elo评分”的正确写法。
• 个别用户如snitty的评论带有调侃性质，偏向个人喜好，未直接参与操作效率的讨论。

44279579.article_content:
Jacob Brazeal
Uncategorized
June 14, 2025
1 Minute
I’ve been playing chess a
long time
now, and I’ve always been a good deal better (maybe a couple hundred ELO points) at blitz (3+0 or 5+0) than bullet (1+0). Well, I may have just fixed that. I changed how I move pieces this afternoon and have gained about 100 ELO already. When I play on a computer, I usually drag-and-drop pieces. But it turns out you can also move pieces by clicking first on your piece and then the target square. An analysis of my recent games indicates this shift saved me about 0.25 seconds per move, shifting from an average of around 1.8 seconds/move to 1.6 seconds/move. I can’t believe I never figured this out before.
The graph above compares a 25-game rolling average of my ELO vs. average seconds per move over the last 100 games. Ithink there are a couple things going on:
click-and-click ™ is physically faster than drag-and-drop, especially when the piece is moving a long way.
click-and-click allows a better alternative to pre-moving, which matters a lot in bullet chess. You can click the piece you think you’ll move before your opponent moves, and then if the move still works, you can instantly click the target square. But if the move actually doesn’t work, then you can avoid the blunder.
It
feels
like I have just enough time to actually think through my moves now.  Historically I’m usually so short on time in bullet chess that I end up pre-moving a lot of the game, or otherwise rushing, with all the associated blunders. This change in mechanics has cut the difference between my blitz and bullet ELOs in half, and I think if I keep playing, the difference will continue to drop.
Has everyone else been doing click-and-click this whole time instead of drag-and-drop? Sheesh!

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于社交媒体平台内容审核和平台责任的讨论

不同观点：
• 观点一：支持对社交媒体平台实施更严格的内容审核和监管。支持者认为，社交媒体平台应为平台上的非法或有害内容承担更多责任，尤其是在涉及未成年人保护和虚假信息传播时。他们主张通过立法或平台自律来确保网络环境的健康和安全。支持该观点的用户常引用现实中的例子，如青少年心理健康受到社交媒体不良内容的影响，以及虚假信息在重大事件（如选举）中的危害。

• 观点二：反对对社交媒体平台施加过多的内容审核责任。反对者认为，过度监管可能会导致言论自由受到限制，平台可能会因为担心承担责任而过滤掉合法的、有价值的言论。他们担心平台为了规避风险，可能会采取过于保守的内容审核政策，进而抑制言论的多样性和创新。有用户提到，平台的去中心化特性使得监管难度大，且可能催生规避监管的技术手段。

• 观点三：强调技术中立和平台中立，主张通过技术手段而非法律强制来解决问题。部分讨论者认为，社交媒体平台应借助算法和人工智能等技术手段来自动检测和处理有害内容，而不是通过法律强制要求平台承担更多责任。他们指出，技术解决方案可以在保护言论自由的同时，减少有害内容的传播。

• 观点四：质疑平台责任的实际执行效果。有讨论者提出，即使立法要求平台承担更多责任，实际执行中可能面临诸多困难，如对“有害内容”的定义不明确、监管资源不足等问题。他们认为，平台责任的实施需要有明确的标准和有效的监督机制，否则可能会流于形式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是平台责任与言论自由之间的平衡。支持严格监管的认为保护社会利益更为重要，而反对者则强调个人表达自由不应受到侵害。
• 另一值得注意的讨论点是国际间的法律差异。不同国家和地区对内容审核和平台责任的法规不同，跨国平台在应对这些差异时可能面临挑战。
• 有讨论者提到，平台的商业模式（如广告收入依赖）可能影响其内容审核的公正性和透明度，这可能是未来需要关注的问题。

data.title: Using `make` to compile C programs
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了在不同系统上编译C/C++程序的基本步骤和常见问题，主要以Mac系统为例。具体步骤包括：

1. **安装C编译器**：在Ubuntu上可以通过`sudo apt-get install build-essential`安装，而在Mac上需要安装Xcode命令行工具。
2. **安装程序依赖**：C语言没有依赖管理器，需要手动安装。可以通过系统的包管理器安装，例如在Debian系统上使用`apt`。在Mac上使用Homebrew，但要注意包名的不同。
3. **运行`./configure`（如果需要）**：有些程序需要运行此脚本来生成`Makefile`。
4. **运行`make`编译**：使用`make`命令编译程序，如果出错，通常是依赖问题。需要根据错误信息调整编译器和链接器的参数。

文中还提到编译分为编译和链接两个步骤，需要正确设置编译器和链接器的环境变量以找到依赖库。例如，遇到`library not found`错误时，需要指定库的路径。

• [jwrallie] 分享了一个无需 Makefile 的简单用法，指出可以直接通过命令行对单文件 C 程序使用 Make 工具，这种方法简化了小项目的构建流程。
